definition_zh: 减少；缩小；降低；使陷入（某种状态）；把复杂之物归结为；约分；收汁；还原；复位
definition_en: to make something smaller or lower, to bring it into a simpler form or a worse state, and in chemistry to add electrons to it
core_image: 一口宽锅里汤汁翻滚，水汽不断散走，最后只剩薄薄一层浓汁挂在锅底
scene: 厨师把一大锅汤留在小火上慢慢收，水分一点点走掉，最后只剩能挂勺的浓汁。 Long simmering will reduce the sauce to a thick glaze.
sceneCN: 这里 reduce 指通过加热让液体变少变浓（第 6 个义项：烹调收汁，把汤汁熬到更少的量）；句意：长时间小火慢熬会把酱汁收成浓稠的亮汁。图中可辨识物件：宽口锅、上升的水汽、木勺、挂勺的浓汁。

pos.zh: 减少；缩小；降低；把……归结为；使陷入
减少；缩小；变浓；（化学）被还原

derivatives.zh: 由 reduce 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「减少；还原」
由 reduce 加已然词尾构成，义为「已减少的；已还原的」
由 reduce 加进行词尾构成，义为「有还原能力的」

由 reduce 加施动词尾构成，义为「还原剂；缩小装置」

senses.title: Make smaller in size or amount
senses.titleCN: 在大小或数量上使之变小
senses.definition: to make something smaller, fewer or less in amount
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在体积、数量或总量上变小变少
senses.example: Insulation reduces heat loss through the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 保温层减少了穿墙而走的热量。
senses.why: The core gesture is bringing something down; the modern everyday sense simply applies that downward motion to quantity and size.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是「把某物带下来」；现代日常义只是把这个向下的动作用在数量与大小上。

senses.title: Lower a price, rate or level
senses.definition: to bring a price, rate, speed or level down to a lower figure
senses.definitionCN: 把价格、比率、速度或水平降到一个更低的数值
senses.example: The store reduced prices by a fifth before the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 节前商店把价格降了五分之一。
senses.why: Prices and rates are quantities on a scale, so the same downward gesture is read as a movement along that scale.
senses.whyCN: 价格与比率是尺度上的量，因此同一个向下动作被读作沿尺度向下移动。

senses.title: Bring a problem to a simpler form
senses.titleCN: 把问题归结为更简单的形式
senses.definition: to restate a complicated thing as a simpler one that explains it
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂之事重新表述为能解释它的更简单之事
senses.example: The authors reduce the argument to a single question.
senses.exampleCN: 作者把这个论证归结为一个问题。
senses.why: A simpler form carries the same content in fewer parts, so reduction here means stripping away what can be dropped.
senses.whyCN: 更简单的形式用更少的部件承载同样的内容，因此这里的「减」指剥掉可以舍去的部分。

senses.title: Force into a worse condition
senses.definition: to bring someone or something into a lower or worse state, often with 'to'
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物带到更低、更糟的状态，常与表示「到」的介词连用
senses.example: The flood reduced the village to a few broken walls.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水使村庄只剩几堵断墙。
senses.why: The downward movement can be read as loss of standing, so the verb also describes being brought low rather than made smaller.
senses.whyCN: 向下的移动也可以读作地位的丧失，于是这个动词也描述「被压低」，而不是「被缩小」。

senses.title: Simplify a fraction in arithmetic
senses.definition: to divide the top and bottom of a fraction by a common number so that the value stays the same but the figures get smaller
senses.definitionCN: 用公因数同时除分子与分母，使数值不变而数字变小
senses.example: Students reduce the fraction before adding it to another.
senses.exampleCN: 学生先把分数约分，再与另一个分数相加。
senses.why: Arithmetic keeps the value while shrinking the written figures, which is the clearest small-scale model of the whole word.
senses.whyCN: 算术让数值保持不变而让写出的数字变小，这是整个词最小尺度、也最清晰的模型。

senses.title: Boil a liquid down
senses.definition: to cook a liquid until it thickens and its volume falls
senses.definitionCN: 加热液体使其变稠、体积减少
senses.example: Long simmering will reduce the sauce to a thick glaze.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间小火慢熬会把酱汁收成浓稠的亮汁。
senses.why: Cooking turns the abstract downward movement into something visible: steam leaves and what remains is denser.
senses.whyCN: 烹调把这个抽象的向下运动变成可见之事：水汽走掉，剩下的更浓。

senses.title: Add electrons in chemistry
senses.definition: to add electrons to an atom, ion or molecule, or to remove oxygen from it
senses.definitionCN: 给原子、离子或分子加上电子，或从中去掉氧
senses.example: Carbon can reduce the metal oxide to the metal.
senses.exampleCN: 碳能把金属氧化物还原成金属。
senses.why: The chemical sense came from the older notion of bringing a substance back to a simpler state: the ore returns to bare metal.
senses.whyCN: 化学义来自更早的「把物质带回更简单的状态」：矿石退回为纯金属。

senses.title: Put a bone or joint back in place
senses.definition: to restore a displaced bone or joint to its proper position
senses.definitionCN: 把错位的骨头或关节恢复到正确位置
senses.example: The doctor reduced the shoulder and strapped the arm.
senses.exampleCN: 医生使肩关节复位，并把手臂固定好。
senses.why: Medicine uses the original 'bring back' reading literally: the part is led back to where it belongs.
senses.whyCN: 医学把最初「带回」的读法用在字面上：那个部位被领回原位。

senses.title: Sum up raw data
senses.titleCN: 把原始数据归纳成摘要
senses.definition: to turn a set of measurements into a few summary figures
senses.definitionCN: 把一组测量值变成少数几个汇总数字
senses.example: The software reduces thousands of readings to a mean and a range.
senses.exampleCN: 软件把上千个读数归纳成一个均值与一个范围。
senses.why: Statistics repeats the simplifying gesture: many pieces become one figure that is easier to hold.
senses.whyCN: 统计学重复了那个简化动作：许多碎片变成一个更易把握的数字。

intro.en: Reduce comes from Latin reducere, 'to lead back', built on re- 'back' and ducere 'to lead'. English shortened the sense to 'bring down' and later added technical uses. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: reduce 来自拉丁 reducere「领回」，由 re-「向后」与 ducere「引领」构成；英语把词义收窄到「使降低」，之后又长出各种专门用法。年代为约数。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead or draw along', the root behind duke, duct and conduct; the idea is direction rather than shrinking.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引领、牵引」，是 duke、duct、conduct 等词背后的词根；其核心是方向，而不是缩小。

items.en: Re- 'back' plus ducere produced reducere, 'to lead back, bring back, restore', as one brings a traveller or a troop home.
items.cn: re-「向后」加 ducere 构成 reducere「领回、带回、恢复」，如同把旅人或队伍带回家。

items.en: English took the word through Old French, first in the senses of bringing back, restoring and leading a person to a place.
items.cn: 英语经古法语引入该词，最初指带回、恢复、把人领到某处。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the verb increasingly meant bringing something to a lower figure or condition, and that reading now dominates ordinary use.
items.cn: 从 16 世纪起，这个动词越来越多地指把某物带到更低的数值或状态，这一读法如今在日常用法中占主导。

items.en: Cooking added the simmering sense, arithmetic the simplifying of fractions, and medicine the restoring of a joint; chemistry adopted 'reduce' for the removal of oxygen, later generalised to the gain of electrons.
items.cn: 烹调加上收汁义，算术加上约分义，医学加上关节复位义；化学用这个词指去掉氧，后来又一般化为「获得电子」。

items.en: First date uncertain for the sense shift: the date at which the 'lessen' sense overtook the older 'bring back' sense is inferred from citation records, not a fixed event.
items.cn: 义项转变的首见年代不确定：表示「减少」的义项何时压过更早的「带回」义，是根据文献记录作出的推断，并非某一个确定事件。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin root and is constantly confused; the second group holds other words for making something less.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一拉丁词根，极易混淆；第二组是其他表示「使变少」的词。

entries.tag: the noun of the same verb
entries.definition: The act or result of reducing, including the chemical gain of electrons; it names the event, not the action of doing it.
entries.definitionCN: 减少的动作或结果，也包括化学上的获得电子；它命名事件，而非执行动作。

entries.definition: Built on de- 'down from' plus ducere: to draw a conclusion out of given premises, which is reasoning, not shrinking.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de-「从……向下」加 ducere 构成：从给定前提出结论，属推理，不属缩小。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus ducere: to lead someone into a state or to bring about an effect, with no sense of lessening.
entries.definitionCN: in-「进入」加 ducere：把某人引入某种状态或促成某结果，与「变少」无关。

entries.definition: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere: to bring something out into existence; the root is shared but the direction is opposite.
entries.definitionCN: pro-「向前」加 ducere：把某物带出来使其存在；词根相同但方向相反。

entries.definition: To become or make less in number or size; it states the change of amount without the idea of simplifying or restoring.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或大小上变少或使之变少；它只说量的变化，不含简化或恢复之意。

entries.definition: To move something down in height, level or rank; it suits a position on a scale better than a bulk of material.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物在高度、水平或等级上往下移；它更适合尺度上的位置，而非成堆的物质。

entries.definition: To remove a portion, especially of cost, text or supply; it stresses the removal rather than the resulting smallness.
entries.definitionCN: 去掉一部分，尤指费用、文字或供应；它强调移除，而非变小后的结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' plus ducere 'lead': the oldest picture is leading something back home.
normal.cn: re-「向后」加 ducere「引领」：最早的画面是把某物领回家。

normal.en: The family runs reduce, reduction, reduced, reducing, reducible, reducer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reduce、reduction、reduced、reducing、reducible、reducer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern sense: reduce costs, reduce the risk, reduce emissions.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代义：降低成本、降低风险、减少排放。

normal.en: The same root leads in deduce, induce and produce, each with a different direction.
normal.cn: 同一词根也出现在 deduce、induce 与 produce 中，各自的方向不同。

normal.en: Chemistry keeps an old picture: ore is led back to bare metal.
normal.cn: 化学保留了一个旧画面：矿石被领回成纯金属。

abstract.en: Picture a wide pot of soup losing its steam until only a spoonful of glaze is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一大锅汤不断散走水汽，最后只剩一勺浓汁。

abstract.en: Picture a long report folded again and again until one small square remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一份长报告被反复对折，最后只剩一个小方块。

abstract.en: Picture a scattered crowd walking back through one gate until the field is empty.
abstract.cn: 想象散开的人群从一道门走回，最后场地空了。

examples.en: Better lamps reduce the electricity bill in winter.
examples.cn: 更好的灯具能降低冬季电费。

examples.en: The committee reduced the proposal to three short points.
examples.cn: 委员会把提案归结为三条短要点。

examples.en: Hydrogen can reduce the oxide at high temperature.
examples.cn: 氢在高温下能还原这种氧化物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ duce（引导）」——把数量往回领，就是减少

root: 拉丁 reducere「领回、带回」= re-（向后）+ ducere「引领」；英语先取「带回、恢复」义，后转为「使降低、减少」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one downward or backward gesture: quantity falls, price falls, a problem is simplified, a person is brought low, a fraction shrinks, a sauce thickens, an ore returns to metal, a joint returns to place, and data is folded into a summary.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一个向下或向回的动作：数量下降、价格下降、问题被简化、人被压低、分数变小、酱汁变浓、矿石退回金属、关节回到原位、数据被折成摘要。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide pot of sauce simmering down to a spoonful of thick glaze.
core.cn: 核心意象：一口宽锅里的酱汁慢慢收成一勺浓汁。

branches.en: DOWN THE SCALE: whatever is counted or priced moves to a smaller figure, from heat loss to holiday prices.
branches.cn: 沿尺度向下：凡可计数或标价之物都移向更小的数字，从热损失到节日价格。

branches.en: FEWER PARTS: an argument or a pile of readings is restated in a form that can be held at once.
branches.cn: 更少的部件：论证或一堆读数被重新表述成可以一次握住的形式。

branches.en: LED TO A PLACE: a village is led down to rubble, and a shoulder is led back into its socket.
branches.cn: 被领到某处：村庄被带到只剩瓦砾，肩关节被领回关节窝。

branches.en: SHRINKING THE WRITTEN OR THE LIQUID: a fraction loses common factors, a sauce loses water.
branches.cn: 缩小写下的或流动的：分数失去公因数，酱汁失去水分。

branches.en: THE ORE RETURNS: chemistry keeps the oldest picture and calls the gain of electrons a leading back.
branches.cn: 矿石退回：化学保留最古老的画面，把获得电子称为「领回」。

intro.en: Reduce is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb root, and both parts are unusually productive in English.
intro.cn: reduce 由一个拉丁前缀加一个拉丁动词词根构成，这两部分在英语里都异常能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere gives duct, conduct, induce, produce and deduce, while re- recur in return, remain and reflect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 duct、conduct、induce、produce 与 deduce，而 re- 也反复出现在 return、remain 与 reflect 中。

items.example: The prefix supplies the backward direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供向后的方向。

items.example: The root supplies the pulling motion.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供牵引的动作。

items.meaning: to lead back; to bring down
items.example: The verb still carries a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词至今带着方向感。

items.structure: reduce plus the action noun ending
items.meaning: the act or result of reducing

The reduced price applies at weekends.

items.meaning: causing a decrease; chemically able to add electrons
items.meaningCN: 起减少作用的；化学上能提供电子的

items.structure: reduce plus the 'able to be' ending
items.example: The fraction is reducible by three.
items.exampleCN: 这个分数可以用三约分。

items.meaning: a substance or device that reduces
items.example: A reducer joins pipes of different widths.
items.exampleCN: 异径接头把不同粗细的管子接起来。

definition_zh: 十年；十年期
definition_en: a period of ten years
core_image: 日历上翻过的十本厚册
scene: 老照片记下了这个街区几十年的变化。 The shop has stood on this corner for a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 decade 指「十年」（第 1 个义项：十个年头）；句意是这家店在这个街角开了十年。

derivatives.zh: 十年的；每十年的
每十年一次的
长达十年的

senses.title: Any period of ten years
senses.definition: a length of ten years counted from any starting point
senses.definitionCN: 从任意一点起算的十个年头
senses.example: The shop has stood on this corner for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在这个街角已经开了十年。
senses.why: Ten fingers, ten years: counting by tens is older than any calendar.
senses.whyCN: 十根手指、十个年头，按十计数比历法还要古老。

senses.title: A named ten-year span
senses.definition: one of the ten-year blocks used to talk about history
senses.definitionCN: 谈论历史时用来切分时间的一个十年段
senses.example: The music of that decade still sounds fresh.
senses.exampleCN: 那个年代的音乐如今听着仍然新鲜。
senses.why: History is easier to hold when it is cut into named blocks.
senses.whyCN: 历史切成有名字的块，才更容易被人握住。

intro.en: Decade came from Greek dekas, a group of ten, through Latin decas and French décade.
intro.cn: decade 经拉丁语 decas 与法语 décade，上溯到希腊语 dekas（一组十个）。

items.en: Dekas meant a set of ten, from deka, the number ten.
items.cn: dekas 指一组十个，来自 deka（十）。

items.en: Decas kept the Greek sense of a group of ten things.
items.cn: decas 保留了希腊语「十个一组」的意思。

items.en: Décade was used for a period of ten days or ten years.
items.cn: décade 曾用来指十天或十年。

items.en: English settled decade on ten years.
items.cn: 英语把 decade 固定为「十年」。

items.en: The word now also labels cultural periods such as the nineties.
items.cn: 如今这个词也用来称呼九十年代这样的文化时期。

note.en: The look-alike group begins with the same dec- letters, and the meaning group measures time in different lengths.
note.cn: 形近组都以 dec- 开头，近义组则用不同长度来量时间。

entries.definition: to turn a code into ordinary language
entries.definitionCN: 把密码转成普通文字

entries.definition: a unit for measuring the loudness of sound
entries.definitionCN: 衡量声音响度的单位

entries.definition: a flat shape with ten straight sides
entries.definitionCN: 有十条直边的平面图形

entries.definition: a period of one hundred years
entries.definitionCN: 一百年的时间

entries.definition: a long period with a shared character
entries.definitionCN: 具有共同特征的漫长时期

entries.definition: the length of time something lasts
entries.definitionCN: 某事物持续的时长

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with ten fingers and end with a block of history that has a name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从十根手指开始，落到一段有了名字的历史。

normal.en: A decade is long enough to change a street and short enough to remember.
normal.cn: 十年长到能改一条街，又短到还记得清。

normal.en: Count ten new years and a decade has passed without a sound.
normal.cn: 数过十个新年，十年就悄没声地过去了。

normal.en: Photographs are the only scales that weigh a decade.
normal.cn: 照片是唯一能称出十年重量的秤。

normal.en: A child of one decade becomes the parent of the next.
normal.cn: 这个十年的孩子，成了下个十年的父母。

normal.en: Dec- at the front means ten, as in ten-sided shapes and ten-year spans.
normal.cn: 开头的 dec- 表示十，十边形和十年都是它。

abstract.en: Picture ten thick calendars stacked in one corner.
abstract.cn: 想象十本厚日历堆在一个角落。

abstract.en: Picture the same corner photographed once every ten years.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个街角,每十年被拍下一次。

abstract.en: Picture a child and then the same face with grey hair.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子，然后是同一张脸生出白发。

examples.en: The shop has stood on this corner for a decade.
examples.cn: 这家店在这个街角已经开了十年。

examples.en: Prices have doubled over the past decade.
examples.cn: 过去十年里物价翻了一倍。

examples.en: Each decade of his life brought a new city.
examples.cn: 他人生中的每一个十年都带来一座新城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decade 记成「得开的」：de 加 cade 像「得开的」，十年一过，旧日子就得让开，新的日子开进来。

root: 源自希腊语 dekas（一组十个），经拉丁语 decas 与法语 décade 进入英语。法语里它一度兼指十天与十年，十七世纪英语才把它固定为十年，现代又用来指称九十年代这样有共同风格的历史时段。

sensesIntro.en: From any count of ten years to a block of history that carries a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 从任意的十个年头，到一段有了名字的历史。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ten thick calendars stacked in one corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：十本厚厚的日历堆在角落里。

branches.en: The first sense is a plain count of ten years from any point.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是从任意一点数满十年。

branches.en: Once the ten years are shared by many, they become a named block.
branches.cn: 当这十年被许多人共同经历，就成了有名字的一段。

branches.en: The same length of time, one measured and one remembered.
branches.cn: 同样长的时间，一个用来量，一个用来回忆。

branches.en: Both senses depend on counting by tens, an old habit of the hand.
branches.cn: 两个义项都靠按十计数，那是手上传下来的老习惯。

branches.en: Naming a decade is a way of saying that a change was shared.
branches.cn: 给十年命名，其实是在说这场变化人人都经历过。

intro.en: Decade belongs to the dec- family, where the number ten is spelled into shapes, spans and measures.
intro.cn: decade 属于 dec- 这一族，数字十被写进形状、时段与度量里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is decem, ten, with decimus for tenth; Greek deka gave the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 decem（十），decimus 表示第十；希腊语 deka 意思相同。

items.example: A decade passed before they met again.
items.exampleCN: 过了十年他们才又见面。
这份报告研究十年尺度的变化。

items.example: The decennial census begins in spring.
items.exampleCN: 每十年一次的人口普查春天开始。
他们完成了一项长达十年的研究。

items.example: A decades-old tree shades the yard.
items.exampleCN: 一棵几十年的老树遮着院子。

items.meaning: a formal word for ten years
items.example: The charter is renewed each decennium.
items.exampleCN: 这份章程每十年续签一次。

items.example: The map changed decade by decade.

latinEntries.example: Decem is the Latin word for ten.
Decimus marks the tenth place in a list.
latinEntries.exampleCN: decimus 表示列表中的第十位。

definition_zh: 指导；引导；制导
definition_en: help and advice about what to do, or the system that steers a moving object
core_image: 老师俯身指着学生的作业耐心讲解
scene: 老师给了她耐心的指导。 The teacher gave her patient guidance.

指导性的

senses.title: Help and advice
senses.definition: help and advice given to someone who needs it
senses.definitionCN: 给予需要者的帮助和建议
senses.example: The teacher gave her patient guidance.
senses.exampleCN: 老师给了她耐心的指导。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常最常用的义项。

senses.title: Steering a vehicle
senses.definition: the system that controls the path of a missile or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 控制导弹或交通工具飞行路线的系统
senses.example: The rocket uses a new guidance system.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭使用新的制导系统。
senses.why: Guiding a person and guiding a machine are one idea.
senses.whyCN: 引导人与引导机器是同一个概念。

senses.title: Official advice
senses.definition: official advice on study or work choices
senses.definitionCN: 关于学业或职业选择的正式建议
senses.example: The school offers career guidance.
senses.exampleCN: 学校提供职业辅导。
senses.why: Institutions turned advice into a service.
senses.whyCN: 机构把建议变成了一项服务。

intro.en: Guidance is guide plus the noun ending -ance, from Old French guider, to lead.
intro.cn: guidance 由 guide 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，源头是古法语 guider（引导）。

items.en: The root meant to show the way.
items.cn: 该词根意为指路。

items.en: Guider meant to lead or direct.
items.cn: guider 意为引导、指路。

items.en: Guide named a person who leads.
items.cn: guide 指带路的人。

items.en: Guidance named the act of helping.
items.cn: guidance 指帮助与指引的行为。

items.en: The word also named machine steering.
items.cn: 这个词也指机器制导。

note.en: Guidance is compared with look-alike words and words for advice.
note.cn: 把 guidance 与形近词以及表示建议的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who shows the way
entries.definitionCN: 向导

entries.definition: a rule or piece of advice
entries.definitionCN: 指导方针

entries.definition: a person who protects a place
entries.definitionCN: 警卫

entries.definition: an opinion about what to do
entries.definitionCN: 建议

entries.definition: help in finding the way
entries.definitionCN: 指路；方向

entries.definition: information on how to do something
entries.definitionCN: 说明；指导

normalIntro.en: Guidance is the helping hand of advice, for people or for machines.
normalIntro.cn: guidance 是建议伸出的援手，既对人，也对机器。

normal.en: She worked under his guidance.
normal.cn: 她在他的指导下工作。

normal.en: The school gives career guidance.
normal.cn: 学校提供职业指导。

normal.en: Children need moral guidance.
normal.cn: 孩子需要道德指引。

normal.en: The missile has a guidance system.
normal.cn: 这枚导弹有制导系统。

normal.en: Ask a teacher for guidance.
normal.cn: 向老师寻求指导。

abstract.en: A lamp does not walk, yet it guides.
abstract.cn: 灯不会走路，却能引路。

abstract.en: Good advice leaves the choice open.
abstract.cn: 好的指导，把选择权留给对方。

abstract.en: Guidance is a hand that points, not carries.
abstract.cn: 指导是一只手，指方向而不是替你走。

examples.en: The teacher gave her patient guidance.
examples.cn: 老师给了她耐心的指导。

examples.en: The rocket uses a new guidance system.
examples.cn: 火箭使用新的制导系统。

examples.en: The school offers career guidance.

dict_mnemonic.text: guidance 是不可数名词，意为「指导、引导、制导」；under the guidance of 是在……指导下，career guidance 是职业指导；动词形式是 guide。

root: 由 guide 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，源头是古法语 guider（引导）；由对人的指路、建议，扩展到对飞行器的制导。

sensesIntro.en: Guidance means help and advice, a steering system, or official study advice.
sensesIntro.cn: guidance 指帮助与建议、制导系统，或正式的学业职业辅导。

core.en: A hand pointing the way without walking it.
core.cn: 一只指路却不代走的手。

branches.en: A teacher leans over a desk.
branches.cn: 老师俯身在书桌旁。

branches.en: A rocket corrects its own path.
branches.cn: 火箭自行修正航线。

branches.en: A student reads a career leaflet.
branches.cn: 学生翻看职业介绍单。

branches.en: People and machines both need steering.
branches.cn: 人与机器，都需要被引导。

branches.en: Personal help becomes an official service.
branches.cn: 个人的帮助，变成正式的服务。

intro.en: Guidance links to guide and its verb forms.
intro.cn: guidance 与 guide 及其动词形式相连。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word came through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，经古法语传入。

items.exampleCN: 我们参加了有导游的游览。

items.example: She is the guiding hand here.

items.exampleCN: 错误的标志会误导司机。

definition_zh: 桩；赌注；利害关系；股份；赌上；用桩支撑
definition_en: a pointed post fixed in the ground, the money or importance risked in a contest or plan, or a share in something
core_image: 一根钉进土里的尖木桩——既是界线，也是押上的筹码
scene: 菜园边的泥土松软，园丁手里握着几根木桩。 The gardener drove a stake into the soil to tie the young tomato plants.
sceneCN: 这里 stake 是「木桩」（第 1 个义项：打进土里的尖木柱）；句意为园丁把木桩钉进土里用来绑幼番茄苗。

pos.zh: 名词：桩；赌注；利害关系；股份

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 holder 构成，义为「利益相关者；股东」
由本词加 out 构成，义为「（警方）监视守候」

senses.title: A pointed post fixed in the ground
senses.definition: a strong pointed wooden or metal post driven into the ground to hold or mark something
senses.definitionCN: 打入地中用来固定或标记的尖木柱或金属柱
senses.example: They tied the tent ropes to iron stakes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把帐篷绳系在铁桩上。
senses.why: The sharp end bites the earth and stands as a fixed point.
senses.whyCN: 尖头咬进土里，立成一个固定的点。

senses.title: Money or value risked in a bet
senses.definition: an amount of money or value placed at risk in a game or bet
senses.definitionCN: 在赌博或竞赛中押上的钱或价值
senses.example: He lost his whole week's pay on one stake.
senses.exampleCN: 他一把赌注输掉了一周的工钱。
senses.why: The coin is fixed like a post: it stays where it is put until the game ends.
senses.whyCN: 钱币像桩一样钉在那里，直到赌局结束。

senses.title: Something that can be won or lost
senses.definition: the importance or value that depends on the result of an event
senses.definitionCN: 取决于某事件结果的重要性或价值
senses.example: Thousands of jobs are at stake in the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易事关数千个工作岗位。
senses.why: What is fixed in place can be gained or lost when the ground shifts.
senses.whyCN: 钉牢之物会随地面变动而得或失。

senses.title: A share in a business or plan
senses.definition: a share of ownership or interest in a company, project, or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 对公司、项目或结果的拥有份额或利益
senses.example: She bought a twenty percent stake in the startup.
senses.exampleCN: 她买下了这家初创公司百分之二十的股份。
senses.why: A stake in the ground marks your claim; a stake in a firm marks your share.
senses.whyCN: 地上的桩标出你的地界；公司的股标出你的份额。

senses.title: A post used in punishment or burning
senses.definition: a post to which a person was once tied for punishment
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用来绑缚受罚者受火刑的柱子
senses.example: In old stories, witches were burned at the stake.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老的故事里，女巫被绑上火刑柱烧死。
senses.why: The fixed post becomes the fixed place of punishment.
senses.whyCN: 固定的桩成为固定的刑罚之地。

senses.title: To risk or bet something
senses.definition: to put money, reputation, or life at risk on a result
senses.definitionCN: 把金钱、名誉或性命押在某个结果上
senses.example: He staked his whole reputation on the new method.
senses.exampleCN: 他把全部声誉押在新方法上。
senses.why: To stake is to fix your value in place and let the game decide.
senses.whyCN: 赌上就是把你的价值钉在原地，听凭结果裁决。

senses.title: To support a plant with a post
senses.definition: to tie a young plant to a post so it grows upright
senses.definitionCN: 把幼苗绑在柱上使其直立生长
senses.example: The beans were staked before the storm arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前豆苗已被架上支柱。
senses.why: The post holds the weak plant upright, as it holds tents and claims.
senses.whyCN: 桩撑起弱小的植株，正如它撑住帐篷与地界。

intro.en: Stake is a Germanic word for a pointed post, and the betting sense grew from the fixed post of a game's wager.
intro.cn: stake 是日耳曼语中「尖桩」一词，赌博义由赌局中钉定的筹码发展而来。

items.en: A root meaning "to stick, be sharp" is generally reconstructed; detail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为词根表示「刺入、尖锐」；细节来源不确定。

items.en: Germanic built words for pointed posts, kin to steak and stock.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形成指尖桩的词，与 steak、stock 同亲。

items.en: Old English staca meant a pin or pointed post.
items.cn: 古英语 staca 指钉子或尖桩。

items.en: The betting sense arose: the wager fixed in place like a post.
items.cn: 赌博义产生：赌注如木桩般钉定。

items.en: Business shares, risk, and stakes in games all extended the same image.
items.cn: 商业股份、风险与赌局筹码沿用同一意象。

note.en: Stake shares sound with steak and stock, and one family with post-words.
note.cn: stake 与 steak、stock 音近，并与桩类词同族。

entries.definition: a thick slice of meat
entries.definitionCN: 牛排；与 stake 同音但词源不同

entries.definition: a thin branch or rod, same sharp-point family
entries.definitionCN: 棍；枝条；同属尖桩词族

entries.definition: supply, shares, or a tree trunk
entries.definitionCN: 存货；股票；树干；音近但词义不同

entries.definition: an upright pole fixed in the ground
entries.definitionCN: 柱；杆

entries.definition: money risked on a result
entries.definitionCN: 赌注；打赌

entries.definition: a formal bet or risk
entries.definitionCN: 赌约；押注，较正式

entries.definition: a part of ownership in a company
entries.definitionCN: 股份；份额

normalIntro.en: Five real hooks for stake and its bets.
normalIntro.cn: 五条真实钩子帮助记住 stake。

normal.en: stake and steak sound the same: meat on a grill, post in the ground.
normal.cn: stake 与 steak 同音：一在烤架，一在土里。

normal.en: at stake means everything can be lost, like a fixed post shaken.
normal.cn: at stake 表示可能尽失，如木桩被撼动。

normal.en: stakeholder: whoever holds a stake holds an interest.
normal.cn: stakeholder：执「股」者即有利害关系者。

normal.en: raise the stakes: drive the post deeper, risk more.
normal.cn: raise the stakes：把桩打得更深，押上更多。

normal.en: Tent ropes and tomato plants both lean on stakes.
normal.cn: 帐篷绳与番茄苗都靠 stake 支撑。

abstract.en: Hear the thud of a mallet driving a post into the earth.
abstract.cn: 听木槌把桩打入土中的闷响。

abstract.en: See coins stacked beside a campfire game, fixed until dawn.
abstract.cn: 看见篝火游戏旁堆好的钱币，钉定到天亮。

abstract.en: Feel a young tomato leaning, then standing straight against its post.
abstract.cn: 感受幼番茄由歪到直，倚住支柱站定。

examples.en: The farmers staked the fence line before planting.
examples.cn: 农民在种植前先沿线打桩。

examples.en: More than medals were at stake in the final match.
examples.cn: 决赛中利害攸关的不只是奖牌。

examples.en: Investors staked millions on the untested technology.
examples.cn: 投资者把数百万押在未经检验的技术上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯得克」——像「死得磕」：桩子死死磕进地里，磕上多少赌注也不挪。

root: 古英语 staca「钉、尖桩」，属日耳曼语源，与 stick、stock 同亲；一般认为出自表示「刺入、尖锐」的印欧词根，确切形式来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: One pointed post in the ground grows into bets, business shares, punishment posts, and plant supports.
sensesIntro.cn: 一根钉入土中的尖桩长出赌注、股份、刑桩与植物支柱诸义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharp post fixed in the ground as a claim
core.cn: 核心意象：作为标记钉进土里的尖桩

branches.en: posts that hold tents, plants, and lines
branches.cn: 撑住帐篷、植物与边线的桩

branches.en: the wager fixed like a post
branches.cn: 如木桩般钉定的赌注

branches.en: what depends on the outcome
branches.cn: 取决于结果的利害

branches.en: a marked share of ownership
branches.cn: 被标记的所有份额

branches.en: the post as a place of punishment
branches.cn: 作为刑罚之地的桩

intro.en: Stake is a bare Germanic noun; its family grows by compounds and the -holder pair.
intro.cn: stake 是光杆日耳曼名词；其词族靠复合词与 -holder 搭配扩展。

latinIntro.en: Stake has no Latin relatives; the sharp-point family is all Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: stake 没有拉丁同族词；「尖刺」词族全属日耳曼语。

items.meaning: a person with an interest or share
items.exampleCN: 每位利益相关者都签了协议。

items.meaning: a police watch from a fixed position

items.example: Collect dry sticks for the fire.

items.meaning: stake body, stake bed of a truck
items.example: Hay rode on the truck's stake bed.
items.exampleCN: 干草装在卡车的桩栏车斗里。

items.meaning: the prize or risk of a contest
items.example: The stakes of the race were doubled.
Grill the steak for six minutes.

items.meaning: a horse race with entry money pooled
items.example: They entered the colt in a stakes race.
items.exampleCN: 他们给这匹小雄马报名了有奖金的赛马。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 holder 构成，义为「利益相关者」
由本词加 out 构成，义为「（警方）守候监视」

definition_zh: 收入；收益；所得
definition_en: the money a person or business receives regularly from work or investments
core_image: 工资单上的数字顺着账本一栏流进来，落在月底的余额上
scene: 月底算账时，最先要看的是进账与支出。 Her monthly income barely covers the rent.
sceneCN: 这里 income 是「收入」（第 1 个义项：定期得到的钱）；句意是她每月的收入勉强够付房租。

derivatives.zh: 由 out 与 come 构成，义为「结果」，与 income 结构相对
义为「支出、开销」，与 income 相反
义为「工资、劳动所得」，是 income 的一种具体来源

senses.title: Money received from work
senses.definition: the money that comes in regularly from a job or business
senses.definitionCN: 由工作或经营定期进来的钱
senses.example: Her monthly income barely covers the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 她每月的收入勉强够付房租。
senses.why: The word is literally what comes in, so its first home is the household budget.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「进来的东西」，所以它的第一个归宿是家庭账本。

senses.title: Money from investments
senses.definition: profit that arrives from savings, rent or shares rather than from labour
senses.definitionCN: 来自储蓄、房租或股票的收益，而非劳动所得
senses.example: Rent from the second flat is his only extra income.
senses.exampleCN: 第二套房子的租金是他唯一的额外收益。
senses.why: Any stream that flows in counts, whether it is paid by an employer or by an asset.
senses.whyCN: 凡是流进来的钱都算，无论付款方是雇主还是资产。

senses.title: A group's or country's revenue
senses.titleCN: 总收入：集体或国家的岁入
senses.definition: the total money that a company or a country takes in over a period
senses.definitionCN: 公司或国家在一段时间内的总进账
senses.example: Tourism provides a large share of the island's income.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业提供了这座岛收入的一大部分。
senses.why: The same metaphor scales up: households, firms and nations all keep a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 同一个比喻可以放大：家庭、公司和国家的账本都是同样的记法。

senses.title: In economics, a flow of money
senses.titleCN: 所得：经济学中的流量概念
senses.definition: in economics, the flow of money received by a person or sector in a period
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中，个人或部门在一段时期内收到的货币流量
senses.example: Economists compare income with consumption rather than with wealth.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家把所得与消费比较，而不是与财富比较。
senses.why: The discipline needs a noun for a flow, and this compound supplies exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科需要一个指「流量」的名词，而这个合成词恰好提供。

intro.en: Income is a native English compound of in and come, first meaning simply what comes in.
intro.cn: income 是英语本土合成词，由 in 与 come 组成，最初只表示「进来的东西」。

items.en: Inncome and incuman described the act of coming in.
items.cn: inncome 与 incuman 描述「进来」这一动作。

items.en: The noun shifted from the act to the thing that arrives.
items.cn: 名词从「进来的动作」转指「到来的东西」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century income was used for revenue from land or trade.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，income 已用于指土地或贸易带来的收入。

items.en: Income tax made the word an everyday term in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪的所得税让这个词成为日常用语。

items.en: Economics gave it a technical sense as a flow measured per period.
items.cn: 经济学又给了它「按时期计量流量」的专业含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -come frame; the near-meaning group holds words for money received.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -come 框架；近义组收表示「收到的钱」的词。

entries.definition: The result that comes out of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结果」，与 income 结构相同。

entries.definition: A greeting given to a guest who comes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「欢迎」，含 come 一词。

entries.definition: Arriving or about to arrive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「进来的、即将到来的」。

entries.definition: A fixed payment made monthly or yearly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「薪水」，指固定发放的报酬。

entries.definition: Money paid for work by the hour or day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工资」，多按小时或按天计。

entries.definition: Money a business or government takes in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「营收、岁入」，更正式。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal come-in reading, the balanced ledger and the tax form.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借字面的「进来」含义、收支账本与税表。

normal.en: Income is simply what comes in, a two-word sentence packed into one noun.
normal.cn: income 就是「进来的东西」，把一个两词句压进一个名词。

normal.en: Outcome is the mirror: what comes out of a process is a result, not money.
normal.cn: outcome 是镜像：从过程里「出来」的是结果，不是钱。

normal.en: Income tax takes a slice of what has just come in.
normal.cn: income tax 是从刚进来的钱里切走一片。

normal.en: A steady income is a steady stream, which is why the money verbs are flow and run out.
normal.cn: steady income 是稳定的水流，所以谈钱会说 flow 或 run out。

normal.en: On a payslip the word sits at the top, above every deduction.
normal.cn: 在工资单上，这个词印在最上面，压在所有扣款之上。

abstract.en: Income measures a door that keeps opening, not a box that is already full.
abstract.cn: 收入衡量的是不断打开的门，而不是已经装满的箱子。

abstract.en: A budget is a story about which direction one prefers to face, inward or outward.
abstract.cn: 预算是一个关于你愿意朝哪边看的故事：向内还是向外。

abstract.en: To live on an income is to let a river decide the width of every bank.
abstract.cn: 靠一份收入生活，就是让一条河决定两岸的宽度。

examples.en: His income doubled after he changed jobs.
examples.cn: 换工作之后他的收入翻了一倍。

examples.en: The family lives on a fixed income.
examples.cn: 这家人靠固定收入生活。

examples.en: Low income often decides which school a child attends.
examples.cn: 低收入常常决定一个孩子上哪所学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「银卡姆」——银卡里的钱慢慢进来，就是收入。

root: 古英语 in「在内、进入」+ come「来」，字面义为「进来的东西」；对照 outcome、incoming。

sensesIntro.en: Income starts as a literal coming in, then widens from wages to investment returns, to a nation's revenue and to a technical flow.
sensesIntro.cn: income 起初只是字面的「进来」，后来从工资扩展到投资收益、国家岁入，再到专业上的流量概念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of figures flowing in and settling at the month-end balance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栏数字流进来，落在月底的余额上。

branches.en: WORK LINE: a job sends money in every month.
branches.cn: 工作线：每月由工作送来钱。

branches.en: ASSET LINE: rent and shares send money in without labour.
branches.cn: 资产线：房租与股票不需劳动就能送钱进来。

branches.en: SCALE LINE: firms and countries keep the same ledger.
branches.cn: 规模线：公司与国家用的是同一本账。

branches.en: THEORY LINE: economics measures the flow per period.
branches.cn: 理论线：经济学按时期计量这股流量。

branches.en: LEDGER LINE: income is always read against spending.
branches.cn: 账本线：收入永远要对着支出一起看。

intro.en: A Germanic preposition of coming in, joined with a Germanic verb, and a small family of -come words.
intro.cn: 一个表「进来」的日耳曼介词与一个日耳曼动词组合，形成一族以 -come 结尾的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin equivalents are in and venire, which gave English words like revenue and invent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的对应成分是 in 与 venire，英语由此得到 revenue、invent 等词。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 归还，由此得到「收益」之义

definition_zh: 行政的；管理的；后勤的
definition_en: relating to the management of an organization or government, or to the routine paperwork and support work of an office
core_image: 一叠表格与一串签字，把一项申请沿着流程往前推
scene: 新老师报到那天，领钥匙、办门禁、填工资单，跑了整整一层楼。 Most of her first morning was spent on administrative tasks.
sceneCN: 这里 administrative 指日常事务性的行政工作（第 2 个义项：办公室里的文书与后勤事务）；句意为她第一个上午大部分时间都在处理行政事务。

pos.zh: 形容词：行政的；管理的；后勤的；由行政当局作出的

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉形容词词尾而来，义为「管理；行政；政府」
由本词的词干加表示人的后缀 -or 构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在行政上」
由同一拉丁词根构成，义为「管理；施行；给药」

senses.title: Relating to managing an organization
senses.definition: connected with the work of managing an institution, company or government
senses.definitionCN: 与机构、公司或政府的管理工作有关的
senses.example: The reform was mainly administrative and changed no policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这次改革主要是行政层面的，并未改变政策。
senses.why: The adjective adds -ive 'tending to, relating to' to the stem of administratio, so it names whatever belongs to the carrying out of management.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 administratio 的词干后加上 -ive「与……有关的」，因此凡是属于「执行管理」这件事的，都用它来指称。

senses.title: Routine office and support work
senses.definition: of the everyday paperwork, scheduling and support work that keeps an office running
senses.definitionCN: 指维持办公室运转的日常文书、排程与支持性工作
senses.example: Most of her first morning was spent on administrative tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一个上午大部分时间都在处理行政事务。
senses.why: In an ordinary office the grand idea of carrying out policy shrinks to forms and schedules, so the word comes to mean back-office support.
senses.whyCN: 在日常办公室里，「执行政策」这件大事缩小成表格与日程，于是这个词就专指后台性的支持工作。

senses.title: Executive rather than judicial
senses.definition: of a decision, court or procedure, belonging to the executive branch rather than to the courts or the legislature
senses.definitionCN: 指决定、法庭或程序属于行政部门，而不是法院或立法机关
senses.example: The dispute went to an administrative tribunal instead of a criminal court.
senses.exampleCN: 这场纠纷交由行政裁判所处理，而不是刑事法院。
senses.why: Because administration also names the executive branch, the adjective marks whatever that branch does on its own authority.
senses.whyCN: administration 也指行政部门，所以这个形容词专门标记由行政部门依自身权限作出的事。

senses.title: Imposed by officials
senses.definition: of a penalty or measure, ordered by an administrative authority without a court trial
senses.definitionCN: 指处罚或措施由行政机关下令实施，不经过法院审理
senses.example: The company faced an administrative fine for late filing.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司因逾期申报面临一笔行政罚款。
senses.why: If the executive can act on its own, its orders need no court, and the adjective flags exactly that kind of measure.
senses.whyCN: 行政部门若能自行行动，它的命令就无须法院；这个形容词标记的正是这类不经审理的措施。

intro.en: Administrative is the adjective of administration: Latin administrare 'to serve, carry out' plus the ending -ivus.
intro.cn: administrative 是 administration 的形容词形式：拉丁语 administrare「服务、执行」加上词尾 -ivus。

items.en: Minister 'servant' is the starting point of the family, and it is generally connected with minus 'less'.
items.cn: minister「仆人」是这个词族的起点，一般认为与 minus「较少」有关。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus ministrare 'to serve' formed administrare, 'to serve, manage, carry out'.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 ministrare「服务」构成 administrare，意为「服务、管理、执行」。

items.en: Late Latin administrativus meant 'relating to management or service' and was built with the adjective ending -ivus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 administrativus 意为「与管理或服务有关的」，由形容词词尾 -ivus 构成。

items.en: French administratif carried the adjective towards English, where it is recorded from the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 administratif 把这个形容词带向英语，英语自十八世纪起有记录。

items.en: Its uses spread from state affairs to everyday office work, and then to measures taken by officials without a court.
items.cn: 它的用法从国家事务扩展到日常办公，再扩展到官员不经法院所作的措施。

note.en: The look-alike group is the word family built on administrare; the near-meaning group holds adjectives for management, for executive power, for bureaucracy and for office clerks.
note.cn: 形近组是建立在 administrare 之上的词族；近义组收表示管理、行政权、官僚作风与文书工作的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the work of managing, the government, or the giving of a drug.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、行政、政府、给药」，是这个词的母词，同出拉丁语 administrare。

entries.definition: A person who manages the running of an institution or a computer system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理者、行政人员」，由同一词干加后缀 -or 构成。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to manage affairs, carry out a law, or give a drug.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理、施行、给药」，与本词共享同一个拉丁词源。

entries.definition: In a way that relates to management or to official procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在行政上」，由本词加后缀 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to the work of managing people or a business, rather than to paperwork.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「管理上的」，偏指管人与经营，而不是文书流程。

entries.definition: Relating to the part of government or a company that puts decisions into effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「行政的、执行的」，强调把决策付诸实施的那一部分权力。

entries.definition: Relating to rule-bound officials and slow procedures, usually with disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「官僚的、繁文缛节的」，通常带贬义，指受规则束缚的办事作风。

entries.definition: Relating to office clerks and their routine writing and filing work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「文书的、职员的」，专指办事员写写记记的日常事务。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb administrare and the phrases the adjective actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 administrare，以及这个形容词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The ending -ive marks an adjective, so administrative describes anything that belongs to administration.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 标明形容词，所以 administrative 描述一切属于 administration 的东西。

normal.en: The family runs minister, ministry, administer, administration and administrator.
normal.cn: 这一族依次有 minister、ministry、administer、administration 与 administrator。

normal.en: Administrative staff keep the forms moving; they do not set the policy.
normal.cn: 行政人员负责让表格流转起来，并不制定政策。

normal.en: Administrative law is the law about what officials may do.
normal.cn: 行政法是规定官员可以做什么的法律。

normal.en: An administrative fine is ordered by an office, not by a judge.
normal.cn: 行政罚款是由行政机关下令的，不是法官判的。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of forms clipped together, moving from desk to desk until every box is signed.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠夹在一起的表格，从一张桌子传到另一张桌子，直到每个格子都签了字。

abstract.en: The stack never decides anything itself; it only makes a decision travel, which is the essence of the office sense.
abstract.cn: 这叠表格本身从不作决定，它只是让一个决定走完流程，这正是「办公室义」的本质。

abstract.en: When the same stamp is pressed by an official instead of a judge, the word turns into its legal sense.
abstract.cn: 当同一枚印章由官员而不是法官盖下，这个词就转向了法律义。

examples.en: The reform was mainly administrative and changed no policy.
examples.cn: 这次改革主要是行政层面的，并未改变政策。

examples.en: Most of her first morning was spent on administrative tasks.
examples.cn: 她第一个上午大部分时间都在处理行政事务。

examples.en: The company faced an administrative fine for late filing.
examples.cn: 这家公司因逾期申报面临一笔行政罚款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米尼斯」——阿德把一叠表格按顺序排好再传下去：行政的、事务性的。

root: 拉丁语 administrativus「与管理有关的」，由 administrare「服务、执行」加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成；administrare 出自 ad-「朝向」+ ministrare「服务」，再上溯到 minister「仆人」。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses of administrative all describe work done behind the scenes so that an organization, a government or its orders can function.
sensesIntro.cn: administrative 的四个义项都在描述幕后把事办好的工作，好让机构、政府或它的命令得以运转。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of forms and a row of signatures that move a request along its route.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠表格与一串签字，把一项申请沿着流程往前推。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: whatever belongs to the running of an institution is administrative.
branches.cn: 管理线：凡属于机构运转的事务，都是 administrative。

branches.en: ROUTINE: in an office the same idea narrows to forms, files and schedules.
branches.cn: 日常线：在办公室里，同一概念收窄为表格、档案与日程。

branches.en: EXECUTIVE: the branch that carries out policy has its own tribunals and procedures.
branches.cn: 行政权线：负责执行政策的那一支，有自己的裁判所与程序。

branches.en: ORDER: an official can impose a measure without a judge.
branches.cn: 命令线：官员可以不经法官直接施加某项措施。

branches.en: SUPPORT: both office senses share the image of work done behind the scenes so that others can act.
branches.cn: 支持线：两个办公义项共享同一画面——在幕后把事办好，让别人得以行动。

intro.en: Administrative is the Latin stem administrat- plus -ive; the same parts also build the noun and the person who does the job.
intro.cn: administrative 是拉丁词干 administrat- 加 -ive 构成；同一批组成部分也用来构成名词与做事的人。

latinIntro.en: Minister, ministrare, administrare and administrativus are recorded in Latin; the deeper Indo-European root of minister is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: minister、ministrare、administrare 与 administrativus 在拉丁语中均有记录，minister 更早的印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: It points the serving towards someone else.
It is the human centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族里指人的核心。

items.example: It supplies the action behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个词背后的动作。

items.example: It is the verb that the whole English family points back to.
items.exampleCN: 整个英语词族都回溯到这个动词。

items.example: English borrowed it with the ending -ive.
items.exampleCN: 英语连同 -ive 词尾一起把它借了过来。

derivatives.zh: 由本词的词干构成，义为「管理；行政；政府」
由本词词干加后缀 -or 构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由本词加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在行政上」

definition_zh: 造成（问题、威胁）；提出（问题）；摆姿势；冒充；放置；（名词）姿势；装出的样子
definition_en: to create a problem or threat; to ask a question; to hold a body position; to pretend to be something; (noun) a posture or a pretence
core_image: 把一件东西摆到台面上，让所有人都看见它在那儿
scene: 新规定给小农场主带来了严重的难题。 The new regulations pose a serious problem for small farmers.
sceneCN: 这里 pose 是「造成、摆出（问题）」（第 1 个义项）；句意：新规定给小农户造成了严重问题。场景要点：问题被摆到台面上、无法回避；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 摆姿势的人；难题（英式口语 a poser）
摆姿势（的）；装样子的
装腔作势的人（经法语回流）
休息；安放（与 pose 同出 pausare 一线）

senses.title: To create a problem or difficulty
senses.titleCN: 造成：把问题摆到台面上
senses.definition: to create a problem, difficulty, or risk that others must deal with
senses.definitionCN: 造成别人必须应对的问题、困难或风险
senses.example: The new regulations pose a serious problem for small farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定给小农户造成了严重问题。
senses.why: The oldest concrete sense is to place something down. A problem that is posed is set in front of everyone, where it cannot be ignored.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的具体义是“放置”。被 pose 出来的问题，就是被摆到所有人面前、再也无法忽略的问题。

senses.title: To ask a question
senses.titleCN: 提出：把问题摆到对方面前
senses.definition: to put a question to someone, especially in a formal or public setting
senses.definitionCN: 向某人提出问题，尤指在正式或公开场合
senses.example: Reporters posed several questions about the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们就延期一事提出了几个问题。
senses.why: A question is placed before the person who must answer it. The same gesture of setting something down, now verbal.
senses.whyCN: 问题被放到必须作答的人面前。还是同一个“把东西放下”的动作，只是换成了言辞。

senses.title: To pretend to be something
senses.titleCN: 冒充：把自己摆成另一个身份
senses.definition: to claim or pretend to be a particular person or type of person
senses.definitionCN: 声称或假装自己是某个特定的人或某类人
senses.example: He posed as a security guard to get into the building.
senses.exampleCN: 他冒充保安进入了那栋楼。
senses.why: A pretender arranges his appearance in front of others, the way an object is placed for display. The identity is worn like a staged position.
senses.whyCN: 冒充者把自己的外观摆到别人眼前，就像把物件摆出来展示。身份被当成一个摆好的位置穿戴起来。

senses.title: To hold a body position
senses.titleCN: 摆姿势：把身体摆成一个造型
senses.definition: to hold one's body in a particular position, especially for a portrait or photograph
senses.definitionCN: 让身体保持某个特定姿势，尤指为了画像或拍照
senses.example: She posed for the portrait with one hand on the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 她一只手扶着椅子，为这幅肖像摆好姿势。
senses.why: Here the body itself is the object being placed. The painter arranges the sitter the way one arranges a still-life.
senses.whyCN: 这里被摆放的对象是身体本身。画家安排坐像的姿态，就像安排一组静物。

senses.title: To place something somewhere
senses.definition: to put or place something in a position, in formal or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到某个位置，用于正式或文学语体
senses.example: He posed the vase on the windowsill and stepped back.
senses.exampleCN: 他把花瓶放到窗台上，然后退后一步。
senses.why: This is the literal root meaning, the one from which every figurative sense borrows its picture.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的本义，所有引申义都是从这里借走那幅画面。

senses.title: Noun: a posture or attitude
senses.definition: a particular position of the body, or a way of behaving that is held for others to see
senses.definitionCN: 身体的某个特定姿势，或为了给别人看而保持的一种行为方式
senses.example: He struck a relaxed pose against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠在墙上，摆出一个放松的姿态。
senses.why: The verb's product becomes a noun: the position that has been placed and is now held.
senses.whyCN: 动词的产物变成名词：那个被摆好、并正在保持的位置。

senses.title: Noun: an affected manner
senses.definition: a way of behaving that is adopted to impress others and is not sincere
senses.definitionCN: 为了给别人留下印象而采用、并不真诚的行为方式
senses.example: His indifference was only a pose.
senses.exampleCN: 他的漠不关心只是装出来的。
senses.why: If a posture is deliberately arranged, it can also be a false one. The visible position no longer matches the inner state.
senses.whyCN: 既然姿态是被刻意安排出来的，它也就可以是假的。可见的位置不再与内在状态相符。

senses.title: To constitute a threat
senses.definition: to be a danger or menace to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物构成危险或威胁
senses.example: The invasive species poses a threat to native birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这种入侵物种对本地鸟类构成威胁。
senses.why: A threat is a problem aimed at someone. It is placed in their path, the same way an obstacle is placed on a road.
senses.whyCN: 威胁是冲着某人来的问题。它被摆到对方的路上，就像障碍被摆在道路中央。

intro.en: Pose came into English from French with the sense of placing. Its family history is tangled: a Latin verb meaning to pause lies behind it, while a different Latin verb meaning to place reshaped it.
intro.cn: pose 从法语进入英语，带着“放置”的意思。它的家族史相当缠绕：背后是一个意为“停顿”的拉丁动词，而另一个意为“放置”的拉丁动词又改造了它。

items.en: The French verb poser is generally traced to Vulgar Latin *pausare 'to halt, to rest', the same source as English pause and repose. The asterisk marks a reconstructed form, not a recorded one.
items.cn: 法语动词 poser 一般被追溯到通俗拉丁语 *pausare“停住、休息”，与英语 pause、repose 同源。星号表示这是重构形式，并非文献中实际记录的词。

items.en: Old French poser meant 'to put, place, set', and also 'to propose', especially in debating. Its placement sense is explained in the next item.
items.cn: 古法语 poser 意为“放、置、摆”，也指“提议”，尤用于辩论场合。其中“放置”义的来由见下一项。

items.en: Latin ponere, past participle positus, means 'to put, place', and its participle is the source of position, positive, deposit, and compose. Old French poser was not derived from it; rather, the similar stems were confused, and poser took over the 'place' sense. This is a documented case of confusion, not a shared root.
items.cn: 拉丁 ponere（过去分词 positus）意为“放置”，其分词是 position、positive、deposit、compose 的来源。古法语 poser 并非由它派生；真实情况是两个词干相似而被混同，poser 于是接管了“放置”义。这是有文献记载的混同，而非同源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 14th century. Early senses include 'to suppose, to put forward', which survives in the phrase to pose a question.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入这个动词。早期义包括“设想、提出”，这层意思残存在 to pose a question 这一说法里。

items.en: The sense 'to hold a position for a portrait' develops later, and the noun pose, meaning a posture, is recorded in the early 19th century.
items.cn: “为画像保持某个姿势”的义项发展较晚；名词 pose（姿势）记录于 19 世纪初。

items.en: Modern English keeps both branches: placing (pose a question, pose a threat) and posturing (pose for a photo, a false pose). They meet in the same image of something set before the eyes.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了两支：放置（pose a question、pose a threat）与摆姿态（pose for a photo、a false pose）。两者汇合于同一个画面：某物被摆到眼前。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for placing, which is the hidden root behind much of this family. The second group collects verbs of putting forward and showing off.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“放置”的动词，它是这个词族背后隐藏的根。第二组收表示“提出”与“摆样子”的动词。

entries.definition: the place where something is, or a point of view. From Latin positio, from positus, the participle of ponere 'to place'.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所在的地点，或一种观点。来自拉丁 positio，再往上为 ponere“放置”的分词 positus。

entries.definition: the way the body is held. From Latin positura, also from ponere, and it overlaps with pose in the bodily sense.
entries.definitionCN: 身体的持姿方式。来自拉丁 positura，同样出自 ponere，在身体义上与 pose 重叠。

entries.definition: to put together, or to calm oneself. Com- 'together' plus ponere 'place': to place things together.
entries.definitionCN: 组合而成，或使镇定。com-“一起”加 ponere“放置”：把东西放在一起。

entries.definition: to put down, or money placed in a bank. De- 'down' plus positus: something placed down.
entries.definitionCN: 放下，或存入银行的钱。de-“向下”加 positus：被放下的东西。

entries.definition: to put something forward for consideration. Present is neutral and formal; pose often implies a difficulty or a challenge.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事提交考虑。present 中性而正式；pose 常含“造成困难或挑战”之意。

entries.definition: to bring up a question or issue. Raise is the common verb for questions; pose is slightly more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 提出一个问题或议题。raise 是提问题的常用动词；pose 稍正式。

entries.definition: to act as if something is true. Pretend is broader; pose as means adopt a false identity.
entries.definitionCN: 表现得好像某事为真。pretend 更宽；pose as 指冒充某个身份。

entries.definition: a deliberate bodily attitude, often used figuratively for political positioning. Posture is the more formal noun.
entries.definitionCN: 有意摆出的身体姿态，也常比喻政治上的站位。posture 是更正式的名词。

entries.definition: to put something in a position. Place is the plain everyday verb; pose in this sense is literary.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放在某个位置。place 是日常平实的动词；pose 的这个义项带文学色彩。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the object placed on the table, the question put to you, the fake uniform, the painter's sitter, and the borrowed pose.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：摆上桌的物件、推到你面前的问题、假制服、画家的模特、借来的姿态。

normal.en: Pose = place. Whatever is posed is put in front of you and stays there.
normal.cn: pose＝放置。凡被 pose 出来的，都摆在你面前，并且留在那儿。

normal.en: Pose a question: the question is physically set down between you and the person who must answer.
normal.cn: pose a question：问题被实打实地放在你和必须作答的人中间。

normal.en: Pose as a guard: you wear an identity the way you wear a uniform.
normal.cn: pose as a guard：你把身份穿在身上，就像穿上一套制服。

normal.en: Pose for a portrait: your body becomes the still-life the painter arranges.
normal.cn: pose for a portrait：你的身体成了画家摆布的那组静物。

normal.en: A pose can be sincere posture or a fake one; the noun covers both the stance and the act.
normal.cn: a pose 可以是真诚的姿态，也可以是假装的；这个名词同时覆盖“站姿”与“做戏”。

abstract.en: To pose a problem is to give it a location; what has no place can be ignored.
abstract.cn: 把问题 pose 出来，就是给它一个位置；没有位置的东西才能被忽略。

abstract.en: Every pose is a claim about where the body ends and the performance begins.
abstract.cn: 每一个姿态都在主张一件事：身体在哪里结束，表演从哪里开始。

abstract.en: The same gesture that sets a vase on a sill sets a question before a mind; placement is the common grammar of matter and speech.
abstract.cn: 把花瓶放上窗台与把问题放到心智面前，是同一个动作；放置是物质与言语共有的语法。

examples.en: The question posed by the audience was harder than any the professor had prepared for.
examples.cn: 听众提出的问题，比教授准备的任何一个都难。

examples.en: The model posed in silence while the students drew her.
examples.cn: 模特静静地摆着姿势，学生们画她。

examples.en: An empty warehouse poses no immediate danger, but it attracts trespassers.
examples.cn: 空仓库本身不构成直接危险，却会招来擅自进入的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: “剖姿”——把姿势剖开摆给众人看，就是 pose（摆姿势）；问题被摆出来，也叫 pose

root: 古法语 poser“放、置、提出”，一般追溯到通俗拉丁语 *pausare“停住、休息”（pause、repose 同源），其“放置”义很可能受拉丁 ponere／positum“放置”影响；英语 14 世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense is a version of placing: a problem placed before people, a question placed before an answerer, a body placed for a painter, an identity placed over one's own. The noun is the position that results.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是“放置”的一个版本：问题被放到众人面前，疑问被放到作答者面前，身体被摆给画家，身份被罩在自己身上。名词则是放置后形成的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands setting an object down where everyone can see it.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把一件东西放下，放在所有人都看得见的地方。

chain: A PROBLEM OR QUESTION PUT FORTH

branches.en: BURDEN: a problem or threat placed in someone's path.
branches.cn: 负担：被摆到某人路上的问题或威胁。

branches.en: SPEECH: a question placed before the one who must answer.
branches.cn: 言语：被放到作答者面前的问题。

branches.en: FALSE FRONT: an identity or attitude arranged for others to see.
branches.cn: 假面：为给别人看而安排好的身份或态度。

branches.en: BODY: the sitter's position and the resulting posture.
branches.cn: 身体：模特的姿势与由此形成的体态。

branches.en: PLACEMENT: the literal act of putting an object somewhere.
branches.cn: 放置：把物件放到某处的字面动作。

intro.en: Pose sits at the meeting point of two Latin families: the pause family from *pausare, and the place family from ponere. English endings then built nouns and agents.
intro.cn: pose 处在两个拉丁词族的交汇处：来自 *pausare 的“停顿”族，以及来自 ponere 的“放置”族。英语词尾再构造出名词与施动者。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere and its participle positus supplied the place vocabulary; Vulgar Latin *pausare supplied the rest and resting vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere 及其分词 positus 提供了“放置”词汇；通俗拉丁 *pausare 提供了“休息、停驻”词汇。

definition_zh: 宇宙；万物；领域；范围；全体
definition_en: all of space and everything in it, or a particular area of interest or activity
core_image: 无数星点在一个不断向外膨胀的巨大黑暗球体里旋转，全部合成一个整体
scene: 天文台的圆顶在夜里滑开，望远镜对准一片几乎看不见的星云。 Astronomers say the universe is still expanding today.
sceneCN: 这里 universe 是「宇宙」（第 1 个义项：整个空间及其中的一切）；句意为天文学家说宇宙如今仍在膨胀。全部星点合为一体的那一整片，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 与本词同源，义为「普遍的；全体的」
由 universal 加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地」
与本词同源，义为「大学」，原指学者的全体
由 univers 加 -ology 与 -ical 构成，义为「宇宙学的」

senses.title: All of space and matter
senses.definition: all of space and everything in it, taken as one whole
senses.definitionCN: 整个空间及其中的一切，被视为一个整体
senses.example: Light from the farthest galaxies has travelled most of the age of the universe.
senses.exampleCN: 最远星系的光已经走了宇宙年龄的大部分时间。
senses.why: Unus is one and versus is turned: all things turned into a single whole.
senses.whyCN: unus 是「一」，versus 是「转」：万物转成一个整体。

senses.title: A field of activity
senses.definition: a particular area of knowledge, activity, or interest with its own laws
senses.definitionCN: 具有自身规律的一个特定知识、活动或兴趣领域
senses.example: In the universe of small business, cash flow is the first rule.
senses.exampleCN: 在小型企业的领域里，现金流是第一法则。
senses.why: A field so large that it has its own laws is felt to be a whole, and the name for the whole is applied to it.
senses.whyCN: 一个大到有自身法则的范围会被感觉成一个整体，而表示整体的名称就被用到它身上。

senses.title: The whole set of something
senses.definition: the complete collection of a kind of thing, without exception
senses.definitionCN: 某一类事物的完整集合，没有例外
senses.example: The survey tried to cover the universe of public libraries in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查试图覆盖全国公共图书馆的全体。
senses.why: Counting every member and stopping at nothing gives the same total that the word first meant.
senses.whyCN: 把每个成员都数上而不留下任何例外，得到的就是这个词最初所指的那个总和。

senses.title: A group of people
senses.definition: a set of people with shared work or interests, such as the art world
senses.definitionCN: 因工作或兴趣相同而聚成的一群人，如艺术界
senses.example: Her paintings are well known inside the fashion universe.
senses.exampleCN: 她的画作在时尚圈里广为人知。
senses.why: People who share a trade form a closed circle, and a closed circle is a small universe of its own.
senses.whyCN: 同行的人形成一个封闭的圈子，而封闭的圈子本身就是一个小小的宇宙。

senses.title: A world of one's own
senses.definition: an imagined or invented world, as in a fictional or parallel universe
senses.definitionCN: 想象或虚构出来的世界，如小说世界或平行宇宙
senses.example: Every novel creates a small universe with its own weather and laws.
senses.exampleCN: 每部小说都创造出一个有自己的天气与法则的小世界。
senses.why: If a whole needs nothing outside itself, an invented one can be complete too, and the word is lent to fiction.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个整体无需外物即可自足，那么虚构的整体也可以完整，这个词便借给了小说。

intro.en: Universe comes straight from a Latin adjective meaning turned into one, and became a noun in French before English.
intro.cn: universe 直接来自一个意为「合成一个」的拉丁语形容词，在法语中先成为名词，再进入英语。

items.en: Unus meant one and vertere meant to turn; universus described many things turned into one whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，vertere 意为「转动」；universus 表示许多事物转成一个整体。

items.en: The neuter form universum was used as a noun for the whole of things.
items.cn: 其中性形式 universum 被用作名词，指万物的全体。

items.en: Old French univers took the noun for the totality of creation, and used it for a whole community as well.
items.cn: 古法语 univers 接纳了这个名词，指造物的全体，也用来指一个完整的团体。

items.en: English adopted universe for the whole of created things, earth and heavens together.
items.cn: 英语以 universe 指被造万物的全体，天地合在一起。

items.en: Astronomy redrew the word as all of space and time, and everyday speech borrowed it for any large field or circle.
items.cn: 天文学把这个词界定为整个空间与时间，日常言语又借它指任何大的领域或圈子。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same one-and-turn root; the near-meaning group gathers words for totalities of different kinds.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「合一」词根上的词；近义组收表示不同类型整体的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning true of everyone or everything.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「普遍的、全体的」。

entries.definition: A place of higher learning; once a whole guild of scholars.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大学」，原指学者的整个行会。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning by all or in every case.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「普遍地」。

entries.definition: The plural, used for imagined or parallel worlds.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，多用于虚构世界或平行宇宙。

entries.definition: Varied and unlike each other; it contains vers but no one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，含 vers 但不含「一」。

entries.definition: The universe seen as an ordered, harmonious whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宇宙」，强调其有秩序的和谐整体。

entries.definition: All that exists, seen as made by a creator.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「造物、万物」，带有被创造的含义。

entries.definition: The earth and its people, or a particular sphere of life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「世界」，也可指某个生活领域。

entries.definition: A kingdom or a distinct area of activity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「领域、王国」，指一个独立的范围。

entries.definition: One of the large systems of stars; only a part of the universe.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「星系」，只是宇宙的一部分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin pieces of the word and the phrases it appears in today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词的拉丁部件，以及它今天常见的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- is one and verse is turn: the whole of things turned into one.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，verse 是「转」：万物转成一个。

normal.en: The universe is still expanding, so the word names something it cannot hold still.
normal.cn: 宇宙仍在膨胀，因此这个词命名的东西无法静止。

normal.en: University carries the same root: one whole community of scholars.
normal.cn: university 有同一词根：一整个学者的团体。

normal.en: A parallel universe is invented; the fashion universe is merely a large circle.
normal.cn: 平行宇宙是虚构的；时尚界只是一大圈人。

normal.en: The universe of libraries means every library, counted together.
normal.cn: 图书馆的全体指把所有图书馆加在一起。

abstract.en: Picture every star turned towards one centre: the word started as an act of gathering, not a place.
abstract.cn: 想象所有星辰都朝向同一个中心：这个词起初是收拢的动作，而不是一个地点。

abstract.en: Any field large enough to have its own rules gets called a universe, because it is whole inside itself.
abstract.cn: 任何大到有自己规则的领域都会被称作一个宇宙，因为它在内部自成整体。

abstract.en: The word is an answer to a question: what is there, if you count everything at once.
abstract.cn: 这个词回答的是一个问题：如果把所有东西一次数完，那里有什么。

examples.en: Scientists still argue about how the universe began.
examples.cn: 科学家们仍在争论宇宙是如何开始的。

examples.en: In the universe of online shops, speed of delivery decides everything.
examples.cn: 在网络商店这个领域里，送货速度决定一切。

examples.en: The novel builds a universe where people can hear each other's thoughts.
examples.cn: 这部小说构建了一个人们能听见彼此心思的世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼沃斯」——优尼把沃斯整个转成一团：宇宙、全体

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」加 vertere「转动」构成的 universus「合成一个的、整个的」，其中性形式 universum 作名词指万物全体，经古法语 univers 进入英语，近代天文学用来指整个空间与时间。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of universe all name a whole gathered into one: all of space, a field with its own rules, a complete set, a circle of people, or an imagined world.
sensesIntro.cn: universe 的五个义项都在命名被收成一个的整体：整个空间、自成一体的领域、完整的集合、一圈人，或虚构的世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: countless stars turning inside one vast sphere of darkness.
core.cn: 核心意象：无数星点在同一个巨大黑暗球体里旋转。

branches.en: THE COSMOS: space and every object in it, taken together.
branches.cn: 宇宙线：空间及其中的每一个物体，合在一起。

branches.en: THE FIELD: one area of activity with its own rules.
branches.cn: 领域线：一个有自身规则的特定活动范围。

branches.en: THE SET: every member of a kind, without exception.
branches.cn: 集合线：某一类里的每个成员，没有例外。

branches.en: THE CIRCLE: a group of people who share a world.
branches.cn: 圈子线：共享同一个世界的一群人。

branches.en: THE INVENTION: fiction builds small universes of its own.
branches.cn: 虚构线：小说造出自己的一方小宇宙。

intro.en: Universe is a two-piece Latin compound, and the rest of its family is made with English suffixes.
intro.cn: universe 是两段组成的拉丁语复合词，家族其余成员由英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Unus, vertere and universus are all recorded, and universum appears as a noun in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus、vertere、universus 均有记录，universum 在拉丁语中作名词使用。

items.example: It closes the Latin adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁语形容词收成名词。

definition_zh: 限制；局限于；禁闭
definition_en: to keep something within limits, or to keep a person in one place
core_image: 一圈低矮的篱笆，把羊群圈在草地内
scene: 医生嘱咐他把活动范围限制在家里。 The doctor told him to confine his activity to the house.
sceneCN: 这里 confine 指「限制」（第 1 个义项：把范围限定在某个界限内）；句意是医生嘱咐他把活动范围限制在家里。

derivatives.zh: 限制；监禁；分娩
受限的；狭窄的
边界；范围
局限的；束缚的

senses.title: Keep within limits
senses.definition: to keep an activity or subject inside a fixed limit
senses.definitionCN: 把活动或话题限定在固定的范围之内
senses.example: Please confine your remarks to the topic.
senses.exampleCN: 请把发言限制在这个话题之内。
senses.why: A boundary makes a discussion sharp instead of endless.
senses.whyCN: 有了边界，讨论才会集中，而不是漫无边际。

senses.title: Keep in one place
senses.definition: to keep a person or animal in a closed space
senses.definitionCN: 把人或动物关在封闭的空间里
senses.example: The prisoner was confined to a small cell.
senses.exampleCN: 那名囚犯被关在一间小牢房里。
senses.why: Walls do to a body what rules do to a topic.
senses.whyCN: 墙对身体的限制，正如规则对话题的限制。

intro.en: Confine comes from Latin confinare, to share a border, from com-, together, and finis, a boundary.
intro.cn: confine 来自拉丁语 confinare，意为共有一条边界，由 com-（一起）与 finis（边界）构成。

items.en: Finis meant the end or the border of a place.
items.cn: finis 意为一个地方的终端或边界。

items.en: Confinare meant to place something inside a border.
items.cn: confinare 意为把某物放进边界之内。

items.en: Old French confiner meant to keep within a district.
items.cn: 古法语 confiner 意为把某物限制在一个区域内。

items.en: English confine first meant to border on a place.
items.cn: 英语 confine 最初指与某地接壤。

items.en: It now means to limit a subject or shut a person in.
items.cn: 如今它指限制一个话题，或把人关起来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that begin like confine, and the meaning group names other ways of setting limits.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 confine 词形相近的词，近义组列出其他设定限界的说法。

entries.definition: to show that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 确认；证实

entries.definition: to tell a secret to someone trusted
entries.definitionCN: 倾诉；信赖

entries.definition: to state the exact meaning of something
entries.definitionCN: 界定；下定义

entries.definition: to keep something within a limit
entries.definitionCN: 限制；约束

entries.definition: to stop something from going beyond a point
entries.definitionCN: 限定；限制

entries.definition: to put someone in prison
entries.definitionCN: 监禁；关押

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a low fence around sheep, then move to a short speech and to a narrow cell.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从围住羊群的低篱笆开始，再走到短短的发言与狭小的牢房。

normal.en: Con- is together and fine comes from finis, a border, so confine is to put a border around.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，fine 来自 finis（边界），所以 confine 就是在四周划出边界。

normal.en: A fence confines sheep just as a rule confines a discussion.
normal.cn: 篱笆圈住羊群，正如规则圈住讨论。

normal.en: To be confined to bed is to have a room the size of a mattress.
normal.cn: 卧床不起，就是把活动范围缩到一张床那么大。

normal.en: Confine and define both carry finis, the word for a boundary.
normal.cn: confine 与 define 都带着 finis，也就是边界这个词。

normal.en: A confined space feels small because the walls are doing their job.
normal.cn: 封闭空间显得小，是因为墙在履行它们的职责。

abstract.en: Picture a chalk line drawn around a pair of shoes.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈粉笔线画在一双鞋周围。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp lighting only one page.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只照亮一页纸。

abstract.en: Picture a bird with a short string on its leg.
abstract.cn: 想象一只腿上系着短绳的鸟。

examples.en: Try to confine your answer to one page.
examples.cn: 尽量把答案限制在一页之内。

examples.en: She was confined to bed with a fever.
examples.cn: 她因发烧而卧床不起。

examples.en: The animals are confined in a small yard.
examples.cn: 这些动物被关在一个小院子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confine 记成 con（一起）加 fine（边界）：四面都划上边界，就是限制；被边界关住，就是禁闭。

root: 源自拉丁语 confinare（com 一起 + finis 边界），本义是共有一条边界，后引申为限制范围与禁闭。

sensesIntro.en: From sharing a border, to drawing a border around a topic, and finally to shutting a body behind walls.
sensesIntro.cn: 从共有一条边界，到给话题划出边界，最后到把身体关进墙内。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low fence draws a circle, and everything must stay inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈低篱笆划出范围，里面的东西都不能出去。

branches.en: Limiting a subject keeps a discussion from wandering.
branches.cn: 限制话题，能防止讨论四处游走。

branches.en: Confining a person or animal removes the choice to leave.
branches.cn: 把人或动物关起来，就是拿走了离开的选择。

branches.en: Both senses draw a line that cannot be crossed.
branches.cn: 两个义项都划出一条不能越过的线。

branches.en: A confined answer is often a clearer one.
branches.cn: 被限制范围的回答，往往更清楚。

branches.en: A confined space is small by design, not by accident.
branches.cn: 封闭空间的小是设计出来的，不是偶然。

intro.en: Confine is built on Latin com-, together, plus finis, a boundary.
intro.cn: confine 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 finis（边界）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin border base fin- also appears in define, final and finish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的边界词基 fin- 也出现在 define、final 与 finish 中。

items.example: Confine the notes to one page.

items.meaning: the state of being shut in

definition_zh: 主动性；主动权；倡议；首创精神
definition_en: the ability to act first without being told, or a new plan intended to solve a problem
core_image: 不等指令先迈出的第一步：自己把球踢起来
scene: 会议室里，主管刚说完问题还没安排人手，一位组员已起身领了任务。 She showed great initiative by starting the project before anyone asked her.
sceneCN: 这里 initiative 是「主动性」（第 1 个义项：没人吩咐就先行动的能力）；句意：没人要求她就开始做项目，展现出很强的主动性。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「开始；发起；使入门」
同根词，义为「最初的；开始的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「开始；入会仪式」
由动词加施动者后缀构成，义为「发起人」

senses.title: Acting first without being told
senses.definition: the ability to decide and act on your own, without waiting for orders
senses.definitionCN: 不等指令便自行判断和行动的能力
senses.example: Solving the customer complaint showed real initiative.
senses.exampleCN: 主动解决顾客投诉体现了真正的主动性。
senses.why: From the root meaning beginning, initiative is the power to begin things yourself.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义是「开始」，主动性正是自己发起事情的能力。

senses.title: The leading position in an activity
senses.definition: the advantage or control that comes from being the one who acts first
senses.definitionCN: 因率先行动而占据的优势或掌控地位
senses.example: The visiting team seized the initiative early in the match.
senses.exampleCN: 客队早早抢占了比赛的主动权。
senses.why: Whoever begins first steers the flow, so beginning becomes holding the lead.
senses.whyCN: 谁先开始谁就引导节奏，「开始」便转化为「掌控」。

senses.title: A new plan or proposal
senses.definition: an important new plan intended to solve a problem or achieve a goal
senses.definitionCN: 为解决问题或达成目标而提出的重要新计划
senses.example: The city launched a recycling initiative last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市去年春天发起了一项回收计划。
senses.why: A plan is a proposed beginning, so the beginning-word names the plan itself.
senses.whyCN: 计划就是一种提议的「开端」，于是「开端」一词转指计划本身。

senses.title: The power or right to propose new law
senses.definition: in politics, the right of citizens to propose a law directly
senses.definitionCN: 政治上公民直接提出法案的权利
senses.example: Voters used their initiative power to put the measure on the ballot.
senses.exampleCN: 选民动用立法倡议权把这项措施推上选票。
senses.why: Lawmaking from below is the citizenry acting as the first mover.
senses.whyCN: 自下而上立法，正是公民扮演「第一推动者」。

intro.en: Initiative traces straight back to Latin words about entering and beginning.
intro.cn: initiative 直接溯源于拉丁语中关于「进入、开始」的词。

items.en: From Latin initiare (to begin), built on initium (a beginning, an entrance), literally a going-in.
items.cn: 源自拉丁语 initiare（开始），建立在 initium（开端、入口）之上，字面为「走进去」。

items.en: Initium joined inire (to go in) with the prefix in-, so beginning was pictured as stepping in.
items.cn: initium 由前缀 in- 加 inire（走入）构成，「开始」被想象为「迈入」。

items.en: French coined initiative in the eighteenth century for the first move in a process or dispute.
items.cn: 法语于十八世纪造出 initiative，指进程或争端中的先手动作。

items.en: English borrowed it in the late eighteenth century, quickly adding the political-plan senses.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪末借入，很快衍生出政治与计划层面的义项。

items.en: Business and government usage fixed the two modern cores: personal drive and official program.
items.cn: 商务与政务用法固定了现代两大核心：个人主动性与官方计划。

note.en: All the look-alikes share the begin-root; the near-meaning words describe acting first.
note.cn: 形近词共享「开始」词根；近义词描述率先行动。

entries.definition: happening at the beginning

entries.definition: to begin or start something

entries.definition: the act of starting something or admitting someone
entries.definitionCN: 开始；入会仪式

entries.definition: energy and determination to act
entries.definitionCN: 干劲；进取心

entries.definition: willingness to attempt new things
entries.definitionCN: 进取精神；事业心

normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词根与词族的联想。

normal.cn: 词根 init- 表示开始；后缀 -ative 使之成为「倾向于开始」的品质。

normal.cn: 同根词：initial、initiate、initiation。

normal.en: Take the initiative: be the one who begins.

normal.en: Government initiatives are plans that begin new programs.
normal.cn: 政府 initiative 是开启新项目的计划。

normal.en: Latin picture: initium, a stepping-in, like a foot through a doorway.
normal.cn: 拉丁画面：initium，迈入门槛，像一脚跨进门。

abstract.cn: 对手尚未落座，棋手已推起了兵。

abstract.en: A raised hand in a quiet meeting room.
abstract.cn: 安静的会议室里一只举起的手。

abstract.en: An open door with footprints leading in first.
abstract.cn: 一扇敞开的门，脚印率先走了进去。

examples.en: Staff who take the initiative are often trusted with bigger tasks.
examples.cn: 能主动出击的员工常被托付更重要的任务。

examples.en: The health initiative aims to cut smoking across the county.
examples.cn: 这项健康倡议旨在减少全县的吸烟现象。

examples.en: After losing the initiative, the team struggled to respond.
examples.cn: 失去主动权后，这支队伍应对乏力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一 foot 醒」——别人还在等，你一只脚已经先踏醒门外的早晨。

root: 拉丁语 initium（开端）由 in-（进入）加 ire（走）构成，字面为「走进去」；initiative 即「开启的能力或动作」。

sensesIntro.en: One idea of beginning branches into personal drive, leading position, new plans, and citizen power.
sensesIntro.cn: 「开端」一个意象分岔出个人主动、先手优势、新计划与公民权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first step through the door
core.cn: 核心意象：跨进门的第一步

branches.en: the personal habit of starting things
branches.cn: 主动做事的个人习惯

branches.en: control held by whoever moved first
branches.cn: 先动者掌握的控制权

branches.en: a packaged plan for solving a problem
branches.cn: 打包成方案的问题解法

branches.en: citizens as first movers of law
branches.cn: 公民作为立法的第一推动者

branches.en: beginning first and thereby leading
branches.cn: 先行开始，因而领先

intro.cn: 这个词是一台小机器：开始词根加形容词后缀。

definition_zh: 恩惠；帮忙；赞成；偏爱
definition_en: a kind act that helps someone, approval or support, or a preference shown to one side
core_image: 邻居隔着一道矮墙递来一篮刚摘的苹果，笑着说不用还
scene: 她帮邻居照看了一整天狗，邻居连声道谢。 He asked me to do him a favour.
sceneCN: 这里 favour 是「恩惠；帮忙」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他请我帮他一个忙。

senses.title: A kind act
senses.definition: an act of kindness that helps another person
senses.definitionCN: 帮助他人的善意举动
senses.example: She did me a great favour last week.
senses.exampleCN: 她上周帮了我一个大忙。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of a helpful act.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示「帮忙」的日常核心义。

senses.title: Approval or support
senses.definition: approval of or support for a plan or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对计划或想法的赞同与支持
senses.example: Most voters are in favour of the change.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数选民赞成这项改变。
senses.why: To favour something is to look on it with approval.
senses.whyCN: favour 某事物就是对其抱赞同态度。

senses.title: Partiality
senses.definition: unfair support shown to one person or group
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某群体给予的不公平支持
senses.example: The coach showed favour to his old players.
senses.exampleCN: 教练偏袒他的老队员。
senses.why: Approval can slide into unfair preference.
senses.whyCN: 赞同可能滑向不公平的偏好。

senses.title: To prefer or support

senses.definitionCN: 偏爱某事物或支持某项计划
senses.example: The committee favours a later start.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会倾向于较晚开始。
senses.why: The noun sense becomes a verb of choosing sides.

intro.en: Favour comes from Latin favere, to be kind or show good will, through Old French.
intro.cn: favour 经古法语传入，源自拉丁语 favere（善待、表示好意）。

items.en: Favere meant to be well disposed toward someone.
items.cn: favere 意为对某人心怀善意。

items.en: Favur named kindness and good will.
items.cn: favur 表示善意与好意。

items.en: Favour entered English as a word for a kind act.
items.cn: favour 以「善举」之义进入英语。

items.en: The spelling favour settled in British English.
items.cn: 英式英语中固定了 favour 这一拼写。

items.en: The word also means approval and unfair partiality.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词还表示赞同与不公平的偏袒。

note.en: Favour is compared with similar-looking words and with words for kindness and approval.

entries.definition: the taste of a food or drink

entries.definition: very strong feeling

entries.definition: the quality of being kind

entries.definition: a positive opinion of something

entries.definition: a greater liking for one thing

normalIntro.en: A favour is a kind act, and to favour is to prefer or support.
normalIntro.cn: favour 是善意的帮助，作动词则表示偏爱或支持。

normal.en: Do me a favour is a polite request for help.
normal.cn: do me a favour 是请人帮忙的礼貌说法。

normal.en: In favour of means supporting an idea.
normal.cn: in favour of 意为支持某个想法。

abstract.en: A small act of help can become a lasting debt of gratitude.
abstract.cn: 一次小小的帮助可能变成长久的感激。

abstract.en: Approval and bias grow from the same root of good will.

abstract.en: Favouring one side always means another side loses.

examples.en: Could you do me a favour and close the window?
examples.cn: 你能帮我个忙，把窗户关上吗？

core.en: Good will shown to someone, whether through help or preference.

branches.en: To choose or support something.

items.meaning: a kind act or to prefer

latinEntries.meaning: to be kind or show good will

abstract.en: Recipes and equations both promise a repeatable result.

abstract.en: No formula can hold a whole life.

sensesIntro.en: Formula means a math rule, a recipe, a fixed method, or a plan for agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: formula 意为公式、配方、准则或方案。

core.en: A fixed pattern that produces a result.
core.cn: 能产生结果的固定模式。

branches.en: Symbols describe a rule.
branches.cn: 符号描述一条规则。

branches.en: Ingredients follow a recipe.
branches.cn: 成分遵循一个配方。

branches.en: A method can be repeated.
branches.cn: 方法可以被重复。

branches.en: A plan gives politics its terms.
branches.cn: 方案为政治提供条款。

branches.en: Equations and recipes share one structure.
