definition_zh: 产量；产出；输出；输出数据；生产
definition_en: the amount produced by a person, machine, or system; data or energy sent out; to produce or send out
core_image: 工厂传送带末端，成品一件件被放到外面
scene: 工厂升级设备后，工程师站在传送带旁盯着成品箱。 Hourly output rose from 120 units to 180 units in the first week.
sceneCN: 这里 output 是“单位时间内的产量”（第 1 个义项：生产出来的数量）；句意：每小时的产量在第一周就从 120 件提高到 180 件。图中可辨识物件：传送带、成品箱、白板、秒表；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 放；置；表达
输入；投入（in + put）
吞吐量；处理能力
输出设备；输出者（技术语境）
外港；输出港

senses.title: The quantity produced
senses.definition: the amount of goods or work produced in a given time
senses.definitionCN: 在给定时间内生产出的货物或工作量
senses.example: The factory doubled its output in three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂在三年内把产量翻了一倍。
senses.why: Output began in 1839 as a technical term of the iron and coal trades: the material put out of the works. The word does not name the goods themselves but the quantity that comes out of the process.
senses.whyCN: output 在 1839 年作为钢铁与煤炭行业的技术词出现：被“放到外面”的材料。它命名的不是货物本身，而是从过程中出来的数量。

senses.title: Energy delivered by a device
senses.definition: the power, energy, or signal that a machine or system delivers
senses.definitionCN: 机器或系统输送出的功率、能量或信号
senses.example: The solar array has an output of five kilowatts.
senses.exampleCN: 这个太阳能阵列的输出功率为五千瓦。
senses.why: By 1884 output named 'energy produced by a device or system'. The industrial image is kept, but what comes out is now electricity or a signal rather than coal.
senses.whyCN: 到 1884 年，output 指“设备或系统产生的能量”。工业画面保留下来，只是出来的东西变成了电或信号，而不是煤。

senses.title: Data produced by a computer
senses.definition: the data, results, or display that a computer sends to a user or another device
senses.definitionCN: 计算机发送给用户或其他设备的数据、结果或显示内容
senses.example: Check the output for error messages.
senses.exampleCN: 检查输出里有没有错误信息。
senses.why: Computing adopts the same schema: a program takes input in and puts output out. The metaphor of a factory becomes a flow of characters on a terminal.
senses.whyCN: 计算机沿用同一图式：程序把输入拿进来，把输出放出去。工厂的比喻变成了终端上流动的字符。

senses.title: Work produced by a researcher or artist
senses.titleCN: 研究者或创作者的产出
senses.definition: the amount or quality of work that a person, team, or field produces
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团队或领域所生产工作的数量或质量
senses.example: Her research output rose after she left teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 离开教学岗位后，她的研究产出增加了。
senses.why: The word extends from things to work: papers, books, and paintings are also what comes out of a process. Output measures volume, while quality is a separate question.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从实物延伸到作品：论文、书、画也是过程里出来的东西。output 衡量的是数量，质量则是另一个问题。

senses.title: To produce or emit something
senses.definition: to produce, generate, or send out goods, data, energy, or sound
senses.definitionCN: 生产、产生或发出货物、数据、能量或声音
senses.example: The speakers output a low hum.
senses.exampleCN: 扬声器发出低低的嗡鸣。
senses.why: The verb 'to produce' appears in 1858, long after the noun. What was a thing at the end of a process becomes an action: the system outputs whatever it sends forth.
senses.whyCN: 动词“生产”义出现于 1858 年，比名词晚得多。原本位于过程末端的“东西”变成了动作：系统输出它所送出的任何内容。

senses.title: Obsolete: to expel or exclude
senses.definition: in older use, to expel or shut something out
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，表示逐出或排除某物
senses.example: The older verb meant to put a person out of a place.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的动词义是“把人赶出一个地方”。
senses.why: The verb is recorded from the mid-14c. in the sense 'expel, exclude', which is now obsolete. The literal 'put out' is the seed from which both 'produce' and 'exclude' grew in opposite directions.
senses.whyCN: 该动词在 14 世纪中期记录的义项是“逐出、排除”，现已废弃。字面的“放到外面”是一颗种子，向两个方向长出了“生产”和“排除”。

senses.title: Creative or athletic yield
senses.definition: the total amount of creative work or performance produced over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内产生的创作或表演总量
senses.example: The band's output slowed during the tour.
senses.exampleCN: 巡演期间乐队的产出放缓了。
senses.why: Output treats creative work as measurable production. The image is quantitative: a career can be counted like a factory shift, even if the value of each piece cannot.
senses.whyCN: output 把创作当成可测量的生产。这个画面是数量化的：一段职业生涯可以像工厂班次一样被计数，尽管每件作品的价值无法这样计算。

senses.title: A signal or terminal that sends data
senses.titleCN: 发送数据的信号或端口
senses.definition: an output terminal, port, or channel through which a device sends signals
senses.definitionCN: 设备借以发送信号的输出端、端口或通道
senses.example: Connect the monitor to the video output.
senses.exampleCN: 把显示器接到视频输出端口。
senses.why: Here output names not the data but the doorway it leaves through. The noun shifts from what comes out to the place of exit, a common pattern in technical vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 这里 output 指的不是数据，而是数据离开的那扇门。名词从“出来的东西”转到“出口的位置”，这是技术词汇里常见的转义方式。

intro.en: Output is a native English compound, first a technical trade term and then a general word for production. No Latin root is involved.
intro.cn: output 是英语本族复合词，先是行业技术词，后成为一般的“产出”词。不涉及拉丁词根。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the mid-14c. meaning 'to expel, exclude', a literal 'put out'. This sense is now obsolete.
items.cn: 动词记录于 14 世纪中期，义为“逐出、排除”，即字面的“放到外面”。这一义项现已废弃。

items.en: The noun appears meaning 'quantity of material put out or produced in a given time'. Until about 1880 it was a technical term in the iron and coal trade.
items.cn: 名词出现，义为“在给定时间内产出或生产的材料数量”。直到约 1880 年，它都是钢铁与煤炭行业的技术词。

items.en: The verb gains the modern sense 'to produce', while the 1884 noun sense 'energy produced by a device or system' follows.
items.cn: 动词获得现代义“生产”；随后 1884 年名词出现“设备或系统产生的能量”这一义项。

items.en: Computing makes output half of the input/output pair. Research and economics extend it to papers, data, and national production.
items.cn: 计算机领域让 output 成为 input/output 这对概念的一半。科研与经济学把它扩展到论文、数据与国家生产。

items.en: The compound stays transparent: out (forth) + put (place, thrust). Something is placed outward, and that outward placement is the output.
items.cn: 这个复合词始终透明：out（向外）+ put（放置、推）。某物被放到外面，而这次“向外放置”就是 output。

note.en: The look-alike group separates out- compounds; the near-meaning group separates quantity from result and from input.
note.cn: 形近组区分其他 out- 复合词；近义组区分“数量”“结果”与“投入”。

entries.definition: the result that comes out of a process. It is the end state, not the quantity produced.
entries.definitionCN: 过程产生的结果。它是终态，不是生产数量。

entries.definition: what is put into a system: materials, data, or effort. It is the mirror image of output.
entries.definitionCN: 投入系统的材料、数据或人力。它是 output 的镜像。

entries.definition: a small military or trading settlement far from the main base. It is a place put out, not a quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 远离主基地的军事或贸易据点。它是被放到外面的地点，不是数量。

entries.definition: the beginning of something. It marks the start, the opposite end from output's product.
entries.definitionCN: 某事的开端。它标记起点，与 output 的产物处在相反的一端。

entries.definition: the act or process of making goods. It names the activity; output names the amount that results.
entries.definitionCN: 制造商品的行为或过程。它命名活动；output 命名由此产生的数量。

entries.definition: the amount produced, especially by land or an investment. It often implies a return on effort or capital.
entries.definitionCN: 产量，尤指土地或投资带来的收益。它常含“投入的回报”之意。

entries.definition: output measured per unit of input, such as per hour or per worker. It is a ratio, not a total.
entries.definitionCN: 每单位投入（如每小时或每人）所对应的产出。它是比率，不是总量。

entries.definition: what follows from an action or process. It can be abstract; output is usually measurable.
entries.definitionCN: 由行动或过程产生的东西。它可以是抽象的；output 通常可测量。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built on 'put out', then three abstract images.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个围绕“放到外面”的钩子，再用三个抽象画面。

normal.en: output = put out: whatever the system places outside itself.
normal.cn: output＝put out：系统放到自己外面的东西。

normal.en: input goes in, output comes out: the same put, opposite doors.
normal.cn: input 进，output 出：同一个 put，方向相反的两扇门。

normal.en: A factory's output is counted in units per hour, like a heartbeat monitor.
normal.cn: 工厂的 output 按每小时多少件来计数，像心跳监护仪上的数字。

normal.en: Computer output is what appears on the screen after the program has put it out.
normal.cn: 计算机的 output 就是程序“放到外面”后出现在屏幕上的内容。

normal.en: Audio output is the sound that leaves the speaker.
normal.cn: audio output 是离开扬声器的声音。

abstract.en: Output measures how much a system gives to the world, not how much it is worth.
abstract.cn: output 衡量一个系统给了世界多少，而不是它值多少。

abstract.en: Every system has a door: what goes in is input, what leaves is output.
abstract.cn: 每个系统都有一扇门：进去的是 input，离开的是 output。

abstract.en: A person can be counted like a factory and still be unmeasurable as a mind.
abstract.cn: 一个人可以像工厂一样被计数，却仍然无法作为一个心灵被测量。

examples.en: The mine's output fell after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，这座矿的产量下降了。

examples.en: Please save the program's output to a text file.
examples.cn: 请把程序的输出保存到一个文本文件。

examples.en: The new turbine outputs twice as much power as the old one.
examples.cn: 新涡轮机的输出功率是旧机的两倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: out（向外）+ put（放）→ 放到外面的东西 → 产出、输出

root: 英语本族复合词：out（向外）+ put（放置）；1839 年见于钢铁与煤炭行业，无拉丁词根。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from industrial quantity, to energy, computer data, creative work, and finally the act of emitting or the port that emits.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从工业产量，走到能量、计算机数据、创作成果，最后落到“发出”的动作或发出数据的端口。

core.en: Finished goods placed outside the factory gate
core.cn: 成品被放到工厂大门之外

branches.en: Measured production: goods per hour, or power delivered by a device.
branches.cn: 可测量的生产：每小时多少件，或设备输送的功率。

branches.en: Computer output and the port it leaves through.
branches.cn: 计算机输出，以及它离开时经过的端口。

branches.en: Human production: research papers, books, songs, performances.
branches.cn: 人的产出：论文、书、歌曲、表演。

branches.en: The verb: a system outputs whatever it sends forth.
branches.cn: 动词义：系统输出它所送出的任何东西。

branches.en: The obsolete literal sense: to put someone out, to expel.
branches.cn: 已废弃的字面义：把人放到外面，即逐出。

intro.en: Output sits in a productive family of compounds built with out- and put. The same two elements also make input and throughput.
intro.cn: output 处在由 out- 与 put 构成的活跃复合词族中。同样两个元素还造出了 input 与 throughput。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entry applies: put is of uncertain Germanic origin, recorded in late Old English as *putian 'to thrust, push'.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁词条：put 的日耳曼来源不确定，古英语晚期记为 *putian“推、刺”。

items.meaningCN: 被放到外面的东西；产量

items.meaning: what is put in: materials, data, or effort

items.meaning: the amount a system can process in a period

items.meaning: a device or routine that outputs data

items.exampleCN: 这台打印机是慢速输出设备。

items.example: Goods were shipped through the outport.

items.meaning: a place or channel through which something leaves
items.example: The river has only one outlet.

pos.zh: 名词：相互作用；交互作用；互动

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ion 构成，义为「互动；互相作用」
由本词换后缀构成，义为「互动的」
由 interactive 加 -ly 构成，义为「互动地」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「与互动有关的」

senses.title: People acting on people
senses.definition: the way people behave towards and respond to one another
senses.definitionCN: 人们彼此相处并相互回应的方式
senses.example: Short interactions at the shop door can make a lonely day lighter.
senses.exampleCN: 店门口几句短短的往来，能让孤单的一天变轻松。
senses.why: It is the noun of action of interact, from Latin inter plus agere.
senses.whyCN: 它是 interact 的行为名词，来自拉丁语 inter 加 agere。

senses.title: Things affecting each other
senses.definition: the combined effect of two or more forces, substances, or systems on each other
senses.definitionCN: 两种或多种力、物质或系统彼此的合成影响
senses.example: The interaction between wind and current shaped the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 风与海流的相互作用塑造了海岸。
senses.why: Science speaks of interactions where a single cause will not explain a result.
senses.whyCN: 在单一原因解释不了结果时，科学就谈相互作用。

senses.title: In scientific research
senses.definition: a measurable effect in which one factor changes how another factor works
senses.definitionCN: 一种可测量的效应：一个因素改变了另一个因素的作用方式
senses.example: The study found an interaction between diet and sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现饮食与睡眠之间存在交互效应。
senses.why: Statistics needed a word for two things acting together rather than separately.
senses.whyCN: 统计学需要一个词指两个因素一起起作用而不是各自起作用。

senses.title: With machines
senses.definition: the exchange between a user and a device or program
senses.definitionCN: 使用者与装置或程序之间的交换
senses.example: Good design makes interaction with the machine feel natural.
senses.exampleCN: 好的设计让与机器的往来显得自然。
senses.why: Software designers borrowed the social word to describe tapping and typing.
senses.whyCN: 软件设计者借用了这个社交词来描述点按与打字。

intro.en: Interaction combines inter- "between", agere "to do", and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: interaction 由 inter-「之间」、agere「做」与名词词尾 -ion 组成。

items.en: Agere "to do, drive" supplied actus and actio.
items.cn: agere「做、驱动」提供了 actus 与 actio。

items.en: Inter as a prefix marked what happens between two parties.
items.cn: inter 作前缀标出发生在两方之间的事。

items.en: Interaction was formed in the eighteenth century for mutual influence.
items.cn: interaction 在十八世纪成形，指相互影响。

items.en: Social science adopted it for the study of persons and groups.
items.cn: 社会科学采用它来研究个人与群体。

items.en: Computing added human-computer interaction, now a field of its own.
items.cn: 计算机领域添上了「人机交互」，如今已是独立学科。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the agere root; the near-meaning group holds other words for exchanges.
note.cn: 形近组共享 agere 词根；近义组收其他表示交流的词。

entries.definition: The verb of acting mutually.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「互动」。

entries.definition: A response to something that happened.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「反应」，对已发生之事的回应。

entries.definition: Doing something, without the mutual element.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行动」，不含相互之意。

entries.definition: The passing of information or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「交流」，传达信息或感受。

entries.definition: The mere fact of touching or meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接触」，只指碰上或会面。

entries.definition: A giving and taking in return.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「交换」，给出去并收回。

normalIntro.en: The hooks hold on to the image of words flying back and forth across a room.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子抓住「话在房间里来回飞」这一画面。

normal.en: Inter- between, act do, -ion the process: doing between.
normal.cn: inter- 在之间，act 做，-ion 过程：在双方之间来回做。

normal.en: Social interaction at the door can save a whole day.
normal.cn: 门口几句交往能救回一整天的心情。

normal.en: Wind and water interaction built the harbour.
normal.cn: 风与水的相互作用造出了这个港口。

normal.en: Human-computer interaction is now taught as its own subject.
normal.cn: 人机交互如今已作为独立学科讲授。

normal.en: Fewer screens means more face-to-face interaction.
normal.cn: 少盯屏幕就多一些面对面往来。

abstract.en: Everything interesting happens between things.
abstract.cn: 一切有趣的事都发生在事物之间。

abstract.en: A conversation is a rope pulled from both ends.
abstract.cn: 一段对话是一根两端都在拉的绳。

abstract.en: Isolation is the absence of a single interaction.
abstract.cn: 孤立就是连一次往来都没有。

examples.en: Regular interaction with teachers helps shy children speak up.
examples.cn: 常与老师往来能让害羞的孩子开口。

examples.en: The interaction of light and shadow gives the painting its depth.
examples.cn: 光与影的相互作用赋予这幅画深度。

examples.en: The app was praised for smooth interaction between pages.
examples.cn: 这款应用因页面之间流畅的交互而受到称赞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特爱克神」——网上互相支持得很神，就是互动

root: 拉丁语 inter-「在……之间」+ agere「做、驱动」+ -ion → 英语 interaction。同族：interact、interactive、react、action。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: people with people, things with things, statistical effects, and users with machines.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：人与人的往来、物与物的影响、统计上的交互效应，以及人与机器的往来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope pulled from both ends, knotted in the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根两端都在拉的绳，中间打了结。

branches.en: THE SHOP DOOR: small exchanges between neighbours.
branches.cn: 店门这条线：邻里之间的小小往来。

branches.en: THE COAST: wind and water make one shape together.
branches.cn: 海岸这条线：风与水共同造出一个形状。

branches.en: THE STUDY: one factor changes another's effect.
branches.cn: 研究这条线：一个因素改变另一因素的作用。

branches.en: THE SCREEN: a tap and a reply count as a social act.
branches.cn: 屏幕这条线：一点一回应被当作社交动作。

branches.en: THE LINK: machines join human social habits.
branches.cn: 连接线：机器进入了人的社交习惯。

intro.en: Interaction = inter- "between" + act- "do" + -ion.
intro.cn: interaction = inter-「在……之间」+ act-「做」+ -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter and agere are attested; the modern noun is English-built.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 与 agere 有记载，这个近代名词是英语自行构成。

items.example: It forms reaction, the one-way cousin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 reaction，只回不互的表亲。

items.example: It allows multi-interaction in new writing.
items.exampleCN: 它使新写作里能说多方互动。

definition_zh: 偶尔的；间或发生的；偶然的；临时凑用的；不定期的
definition_en: happening or appearing from time to time rather than regularly, arising by chance, and made or kept for only a particular occasion
core_image: 一扇老木门整年关着，门轴上的灰积了薄薄一层
scene: 旧书店的卷帘门一年只拉起几次，门口的招牌褪了色，附近的人倒都记得它。 An occasional customer still pushes the door open on Saturday mornings.
sceneCN: 这里的 occasional 是「偶尔的」（第 1 个义项：隔一段时间才发生一次）；句意为偶尔仍有顾客在星期六上午推门进来。图中可辨识物件：卷帘门、褪色招牌、门轴上的灰。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 occasio（时机、机会）经古法语进入英语，义为「场合；时机」
由 occasional 加 -ly 构成，义为「偶尔地；间或」
由 occasional 加 -ness 构成，义为「偶发性；不经常的状态」

senses.title: Happening from time to time
senses.definition: happening or appearing now and then, with gaps of time in between, rather than in a steady pattern
senses.definitionCN: 时而发生或出现，中间隔着一段段时间，而不是稳定持续地进行
senses.example: She made occasional visits to the village where she grew up.
senses.exampleCN: 她偶尔回一趟自己长大的村子。
senses.why: The Latin stem occasio named a moment that befalls a person, so an occasional event is one that only lands on certain moments instead of staying.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干 occasio 指落到某人头上的某个时刻，所以 occasional 的事情只是在某些时刻落到眼前，而不是一直停在那里。

senses.title: Arising by chance rather than by plan
senses.definition: coming about because of chance circumstances, not because someone arranged or intended it
senses.definitionCN: 因偶然情况而发生，而不是有人安排或有意为之
senses.example: An occasional meeting at the station led to a long friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 在车站的一次偶然相遇带来了一段长久的友谊。
senses.why: Since occasio could mean a lucky or unlucky turn of events, the adjective also describes what simply happens to us, without a plan behind it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 occasio 也可指运气好坏的一次转折，这个形容词便也能描述不由计划、只是落到我们头上的事。

senses.title: Kept or used only for a particular occasion
senses.titleCN: 临时的；应景的；备用凑用的
senses.definition: made, kept or used only now and then, for a special purpose, such as a chair set out when guests come
senses.definitionCN: 只为隔一段时间出现的特定用途而制作、保存或使用，例如来客时才摆出的椅子
senses.example: They kept an occasional table folded against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们家里有一张折叠着靠墙放的备用小桌。
senses.why: Furniture that comes out only on certain occasions took the adjective as a name, because the object leads the same intermittent life as the event.
senses.whyCN: 只在某些场合才搬出来的家具也用这个形容词命名，因为物件过着和「偶尔发生的事」同样断续的生活。

senses.title: Not regular in time or amount
senses.definition: not fixed to a schedule, so it cannot be counted on to appear at set intervals
senses.definitionCN: 没有固定排期，因此不能指望它按固定间隔出现
senses.example: The clinic offers occasional free checks for older residents.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为老年居民不定期提供免费检查。
senses.why: Once a thing happens only on some occasions, nothing about it can be regular, so the word also denies a timetable without denying that it happens at all.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然只在某些时候发生，就谈不上规律，于是这个词否定的是时刻表，而不是它会发生。

intro.en: Occasional is an English adjective built on occasion, whose Latin stem names a moment that falls to someone; the whole family turns on the idea of something that arrives rather than continues.
intro.cn: occasional 是英语在 occasion 之上构成的形容词，其拉丁词干指「落到某人头上的时刻」；这一族词都围绕「降临而非持续」这个想法。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall, and it is the source of many English words about things that happen, befall or simply drop.
items.cn: cadere 意为落下，是英语中一大批表示「发生、降临、跌落」的词来源。

items.en: Ob- plus cadere gave occidere, to fall toward or upon something, used of the sun going down and of events coming to a person.
items.cn: ob- 与 cadere 合成 occidere，意为「朝某物落下、落到某物上」，既用于太阳西沉，也用于事件临到某人。

items.en: Occasio named the moment when something falls into place, hence an opportunity or an occasion; it was also the name of a Roman goddess of the opportune moment.
items.cn: occasio 指事情正好落定的那个时刻，因此是「机会、场合」；它也是罗马神话中「恰当时机」女神的名字。

items.en: Old French kept occasion as a word for a chance, a cause or a particular time, and English borrowed it in that bundle of senses.
items.cn: 古法语保留 occasion，指机会、缘由或特定的时刻，英语把这几个意思一并借了进来。

items.en: English added the adjective ending -al to occasion, so occasional first meant 'belonging to an occasion' and then 'happening only on some occasions'.
items.cn: 英语给 occasion 加上形容词后缀 -al，于是 occasional 先表示「属于某一场合的」，后来才表示「只在某些场合发生的」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for a falling moment; the near-meaning group collects words for things that happen rarely or unevenly.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「落下的时刻」这一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示稀少或断续发生的词。

entries.definition: A particular time when something happens, or a reason for doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的特定时刻，或做某事的缘由。

entries.definition: Now and then, at times that are not regular.
entries.definitionCN: 时而；不定时地。

entries.definition: A rhythm or flow, especially of sound or speech, from the Latin word for falling.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指声音或话语的节律，源自拉丁语中「落下」的词。

entries.definition: Something that happens by chance and is not planned.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然发生、并非计划中的事；事故。

entries.definition: Happening only here and there, in scattered and unpredictable moments.
entries.definitionCN: 零散发生、时地不可预测的。

entries.definition: Stopping and starting again at intervals rather than running continuously.
entries.definitionCN: 时断时续，而不是连续进行的。

entries.definition: Not happening often, so that long gaps lie between the times it does.
entries.definitionCN: 不常发生，发生的间隔很长。

entries.definition: Not following a fixed pattern or timetable.
entries.definitionCN: 不按固定规律或时刻表进行的。

normalIntro.en: The word is occasion wearing the adjective ending -al, so every hook comes back to the picture of a moment that only sometimes falls into place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 occasion 穿上形容词后缀 -al，所以每条记忆钩子都回到「只有某些时候才正好落定」的画面。

normal.en: Occasion is the noun behind the adjective, and -al simply means 'belonging to', so occasional belongs to certain occasions only.
normal.cn: occasion 是这个形容词背后的名词，-al 只表示「属于……的」，所以 occasional 只属于某些场合。

normal.en: Occasio in Latin was the moment something fell into place, which links the word to cadere, to fall.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 occasio 是事情正好落定的那一刻，这把它与 cadere（落下）连在一起。

normal.en: Occasionally is just occasional plus -ly, the plain adverb for now and then.
normal.cn: occasionally 只是 occasional 加 -ly，就是表示「时而」的普通副词。

normal.en: An occasional chair or table is an object kept for the times guests arrive, so furniture carries the same intermittent habit.
normal.cn: occasional chair 或 occasional table 是为来客时才用的物件，于是家具也带着同样「时有时无」的习性。

normal.en: In occasional showers, the adjective softens the forecast: rain will come, but not steadily.
normal.cn: 在 occasional showers 里，这个形容词软化了预报：雨会下，但不会连绵不断。

abstract.en: An occasional thing is defined less by what it is than by the size of the gaps around it.
abstract.cn: 偶尔发生的事，与其说由它本身定义，不如说由它周围的空隙大小定义。

abstract.en: Calling a moment an occasion admits that time is not a line but a series of landings.
abstract.cn: 把某一刻称作 occasion，就是承认时间不是一条直线，而是一连串的落点。

abstract.en: A word built on 'falling' reminds us that what happens to us often arrives rather than gets arranged.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在「落下」之上的词提醒人：落到我们头上的事，多半是降临，而不是安排。

examples.en: He still makes occasional trips to the coast to fish.
examples.cn: 他仍偶尔去海边钓鱼。

examples.en: Occasional heavy rain slowed the harvest but did not stop it.
examples.cn: 偶尔的大雨拖慢了收割，却没有让它停下来。

examples.en: The spare room has an occasional bed for guests.
examples.cn: 备用房间里有一张供客人临时使用的床。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶开身」——身子偶尔才开一次门，平时都关着；记住 occasional 是偶尔的。

root: 由 occasion 加形容词后缀 -al 构成；occasion 来自拉丁语 occasio（时机、机会），其词干 occidere 意为「落到某物上」，再上溯 cadere（落下）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a moment that only sometimes falls into place; from it come chance happenings, objects kept for such moments, and the plain denial of a regular schedule.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是只有某些时候才落定的一个时刻；由此分出偶然发生的事、为这种时刻留着的物件，以及「没有固定排期」这一层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old wooden door that stays shut all year, with a thin layer of dust on its hinge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇老木门整年关着，门轴上积着一层薄灰。

branches.en: a shop door raised on a few Saturday mornings
branches.cn: 几个星期六上午才拉起的店门

branches.en: two strangers meeting at a station by luck
branches.cn: 两个陌生人在车站碰巧相遇

branches.en: a folding table kept against the wall for guests
branches.cn: 靠墙收着、来客才用的折叠桌

branches.en: a clinic with no fixed day for free checks
branches.cn: 没有固定免费检查日的诊所

branches.en: the same irregular rhythm seen in events and in services
branches.cn: 事件与服务中同一种不规则的节奏

intro.en: The word is a Latin moment-noun plus an English adjective ending; behind the noun sit a prefix and a verb of falling.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁语「时刻」名词加一个英语形容词后缀构成；名词背后还有一个前缀和表示「落下」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere, occidere and occasio are all recorded, and they give the family its picture of something falling into place at a certain moment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere、occidere、occasio 都有记录，为这一族词提供了「某物在某一刻落定」的画面。

definition_zh: 杰出的；明亮的；极好的
definition_en: extremely clever or good
core_image: 聚光灯下闪耀的宝石
scene: 灯下的宝石闪着耀眼的光。 The brilliant gem caught every eye in the room.

出色地；明亮地

senses.title: Extremely clever
senses.definition: extremely clever or skilled
senses.definitionCN: 极其聪明或技艺高超
senses.example: She is a brilliant scientist.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位杰出的科学家。
senses.why: This is the most common sense today.
senses.whyCN: 这是今天最常用的义项。

senses.title: Very bright
senses.definition: very bright and shining
senses.definitionCN: 非常明亮闪耀
senses.example: The brilliant gem caught every eye in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 灯下的宝石耀眼夺目。
senses.why: The light sense came first, from shining gems.
senses.whyCN: 光的义项最早，来自闪耀的宝石。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: extremely good or enjoyable
senses.definitionCN: 非常好或令人愉快
senses.example: The show was brilliant.
senses.exampleCN: 演出棒极了。
senses.why: Excellence in mind widened to excellence of any kind.
senses.whyCN: 才智上的卓越扩展为任何方面的卓越。

intro.en: Brilliant came from French and Italian words for shining.
intro.cn: brilliant 来自法语与意大利语中表示闪耀的词。

items.en: brillare meant to shine like a gem.
items.cn: brillare 指像宝石一样闪耀。

items.en: brillant described a sparkling stone.
items.cn: brillant 形容闪光的石头。

items.en: English brilliant named a cut diamond.
items.cn: 英语 brilliant 指切割过的钻石。

items.en: brilliant meant very clever.
items.cn: brilliant 指非常聪明。

items.en: brilliant covers light, talent and praise.
items.cn: 如今 brilliant 兼指光、才华与赞美。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the br- or -ill- shape; the near-meaning group gives other words of praise.
note.cn: 形近组共用 br- 或 -ill- 的外形；近义组是其他表示赞美的词。

entries.definition: a thousand million
entries.definitionCN: 十亿

entries.definition: hard but easily broken
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的

entries.definition: the top edge of a container
entries.definitionCN: 边缘

entries.definition: much better than others
entries.definitionCN: 杰出的

entries.definition: so bright that it hurts the eyes
entries.definitionCN: 耀眼的

entries.definition: of the very best quality

normalIntro.en: Brilliant first meant shining like a gem, then shining like a mind.
normalIntro.cn: brilliant 先指像宝石一样发亮，后指头脑一样闪耀。

normal.en: She had a brilliant idea.
normal.cn: 她有个绝妙的主意。

normal.en: The diamond was brilliant.
normal.cn: 那颗钻石耀眼夺目。

normal.en: The show was brilliant.
normal.cn: 演出棒极了。

normal.en: The noun is brilliance.
normal.cn: 名词是 brilliance。

normal.en: The adverb is brilliantly.
normal.cn: 副词是 brilliantly。

abstract.en: See a gem under a spotlight.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯下的一颗宝石。

abstract.en: See a mind light up with an answer.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头脑因答案而亮起。

abstract.en: See a crowd stand and clap.
abstract.cn: 想象全场起立鼓掌。

senses.title: Toothed wheel
senses.definition: a wheel with teeth that turns another wheel and passes power

senses.title: Speed setting
senses.definition: one of the settings that control a vehicle's speed and power

senses.example: He changed gear on the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 他在山坡上换了挡。

senses.title: Equipment
senses.definition: the clothes and tools needed for an activity

senses.example: They packed their climbing gear.

senses.why: The word extends from machinery to personal kit.

senses.title: Adjust to fit

definition_zh: 衣领；领子；项圈；环状物；抓住某人；给…戴上项圈；扭住
definition_en: the part of a shirt, coat, or dress that fits around the neck, or a band put around an animal's neck; as a verb, to seize someone by the collar or catch someone
core_image: 脖子上的那一圈：衣服收拢脖颈的边缘，或套在动物颈上的环带
scene: 小狗在院子里飞奔，主人举起一根红绳子，说： He bent down to fasten the collar around the dog's neck before their evening walk.
sceneCN: 这里 collar 是「项圈」（第 3 个义项：套在动物颈部的环带）；句意是遛狗前主人弯腰给狗扣好项圈，画面聚焦在脖子上那一圈东西。

senses.title: The neck part of a garment
senses.definition: the folded part of a shirt, coat, or dress that fits around the neck
senses.definitionCN: 衬衫、外套或连衣裙中围住颈部的部分
senses.example: He turned up his coat collar against the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 他竖起大衣领子挡风。
senses.why: The neck is where a garment gathers and closes, so the encircling edge becomes the word's first image.
senses.whyCN: 颈部是衣服收拢、闭合的位置，围合脖子的边缘自然成为这个词最早的核心意象。

senses.title: A band for identification or restraint around a neck
senses.definition: a band worn around the neck, such as a pet's collar or a marked band
senses.definitionCN: 戴在颈部的环带，如宠物项圈或标识环
senses.example: The bird was fitted with a numbered plastic collar.
senses.exampleCN: 这只鸟被套上了带编号的塑料颈环。
senses.why: Anything that encircles the neck shares the collar shape, so the image extends from clothing to bands.
senses.whyCN: 凡是围住颈部的环形物都与衣领形状相同，意象从衣服自然延伸到环带。

senses.title: A collar for an animal
senses.definition: a leather or fabric band fastened around a dog or other animal's neck, often holding a tag or leash
senses.definitionCN: 拴在狗或其他动物颈部的皮带或布带，常挂标签或牵引绳
senses.example: She bought a red collar with a small bell for her cat.
senses.exampleCN: 她给猫买了一个挂小铃铛的红色项圈。
senses.why: Sense 02 narrows to animals: the band becomes a tool for controlling and identifying the pet.
senses.whyCN: 由第 02 义项收窄到动物：环带从装饰变为控制和辨认宠物的工具。

senses.title: A ring-shaped part of a machine
senses.definition: a ring or flange on a shaft, pipe, or machine part that holds something in place
senses.definitionCN: 轴、管或机械零件上的环形或凸缘部件，用于定位固定
senses.example: A steel collar keeps the wheel fixed on the axle.
senses.exampleCN: 一个钢制轴环把车轮固定在轴上。
senses.why: Machines use collars to clamp round parts, reusing the encircling image in an engineering sense.
senses.whyCN: 机械用环箍住圆形部件，「围合」意象在工程领域得到复用。

senses.title: To seize someone by the collar
senses.definition: to grab a person by the neck or collar of clothing, especially to stop or hold them
senses.definitionCN: 抓住某人的颈部或衣领，尤指为了拦住或控制对方
senses.example: The guard collared the boy who tried to sneak in.
senses.exampleCN: 保安扭住了那个想溜进去的男孩。
senses.why: The noun names the grabbing point at the neck; turning it into a verb makes the collar the handle of arrest.
senses.whyCN: 名词标记的是颈部的抓握点；名词转动词后，衣领成了捉人的把手。

senses.title: To stop and talk to someone
senses.definition: to catch someone and make them listen or talk, often when they are in a hurry
senses.definitionCN: 拦住某人使其听自己说话，常指对方正赶时间时
senses.example: I got collared by my neighbor in the hallway and heard her whole story.
senses.exampleCN: 我在楼道里被邻居截住，听她讲了半天。
senses.why: Metaphorically grabbing a person's collar to detain them extends physical seizure into social interception.
senses.whyCN: 把「抓住衣领」的物理动作隐喻为「拦下说话」，捉拿意象延伸到社交场合。

senses.title: To put a collar on an animal
senses.definition: to fasten a collar around an animal's neck
senses.definitionCN: 给动物颈部扣上项圈
senses.example: All dogs in the park must be collared and tagged.
senses.exampleCN: 公园里所有的狗都必须戴上项圈并挂牌。
senses.why: The animal collar of sense 03 becomes an action: fitting the band is routine care and legal duty.
senses.whyCN: 第 03 义项的动物项圈转为动作：戴上项圈成为日常照料与规范要求。

senses.title: White-collar and blue-collar social labels
senses.definition: used in compounds to classify workers by the color of shirt they traditionally wore
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词，按传统衬衫领色划分劳动者类型
senses.example: White-collar jobs usually happen in offices, not on factory floors.
senses.exampleCN: 白领工作通常在办公室进行，而不是在车间。
senses.why: The visible part of a work shirt, its collar, becomes a metonymy for whole classes of workers.
senses.whyCN: 工作衬衫最显眼的部分——衣领——借代为整个劳动者阶层的标签。

intro.en: Collar goes back through Old French coler to Latin collum, the neck, so the word has always named what encircles the neck.
intro.cn: collar 经古法语 coler 上溯至拉丁语 collum（颈、脖），这个词从一开始就指「围住颈部的东西」。

items.en: A root usually reconstructed as *kwolh₁- or related *kwel-, meaning to turn or revolve, giving roundness as a core idea.
items.cn: 一般认为源自重构词根 *kwolh₁-（与 *kwel- 相关），意为「转动、旋转」，由此带来「圆形、环状」的核心概念。

items.en: Collum meant the neck, the body part that connects head and shoulders; derivatives like collare (neckband) already pointed to things worn there.
items.cn: 拉丁语 collum 意为「颈部」，即连接头与肩的部位；其派生词 collare（颈带）已指戴在颈上的东西。

items.en: Coler or colier meant the neck of a garment and also a neckband, passing into English after the Norman Conquest.
items.cn: 古法语 coler／colier 指衣服的领部及颈带，随诺曼征服进入英语。

items.en: First attested in Middle English around 1300 as the neck part of a garment, the everyday clothing sense.
items.cn: 中古英语约 1300 年首次见于记载，指衣服的领部，即日常衣着义。

items.en: The verb senses of seizing by the collar and detaining someone developed from the noun image.
items.cn: 16 至 17 世纪，由名词意象发展出「抓住领口」「拦住某人」等动词义。

items.en: Industrial and social extensions appeared: machine collars, and the white-collar versus blue-collar class labels of the late 19th and 20th centuries.
items.cn: 近现代出现工程与社会的延伸：机械轴环，以及 19 世纪末以来「白领／蓝领」的阶层标签。

note.en: Words that look or sound like collar, and words close to its neck-related meaning.
note.cn: 与 collar 形近音近的词，以及意义相关的「颈部、环带、抓住」类词。

abstract.en: The collar is the handle by which the world grabs you or you grab it.

abstract.en: A collar marks belonging: pet to owner, worker to class, wheel to axle.

examples.en: Remember to fasten the collar on your dog before the walk.

sensesIntro.en: From the garment collar at the neck, the word widens to any encircling band, narrows to animal collars and machine rings, and turns verbal for grabbing and detaining.

branches.en: bands worn around necks, especially animal collars

branches.en: engineering rings that clamp round parts

branches.en: grabbing or stopping a person by the collar image

definition_en: a mark or line left by something that passed, or to follow such marks
core_image: 雪地里一串脚印：谁经过，地就记下谁
scene: 运动会清晨，选手们陆续进场，在环形跑道上做起热身：猎人蹲下身，用手指沿着雪地上一串清晰的足迹，一路望向树林深处刚留下的 track。
sceneCN: 这里 track 是「足迹」（第 1 个义项：经过者留下的痕迹）；句意是猎人顺着雪地足迹望向树林。

collocations.zh: 走在正确的路上；思路对头
忘了时间；忘记时间流逝

derivatives.zh: 由动词 track 加现在分词构成，义为「追踪；跟踪定位」

senses.title: A mark or line left by a moving person, animal, or thing
senses.definition: marks or a line left on the ground by something that has passed
senses.definitionCN: 经过者在地面上留下的痕迹或压出的线
senses.example: The police followed the tracks in the snow to the cabin.
senses.exampleCN: 警察顺着雪地里的足迹追到小屋。
senses.why: The core image is the ground recording whoever passes, which is the literal track.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是地面记录下每一个经过者，这正是 track 的本义。

senses.title: A pair of rails or a course for racing
senses.definition: rails on which trains run, or a path prepared for racing
senses.definitionCN: 火车行驶的铁轨，或供赛跑用的专用跑道
senses.example: The high-speed train glides along the new track.
senses.exampleCN: 高速列车沿新轨道滑行。
senses.why: A line left by wheels hardened into rails, so a course for running kept the same name.
senses.whyCN: 车轮压出的线硬化成铁轨，赛跑的专用道沿用了同一个名字。

senses.title: A path or rough road
senses.definition: a rough path or road across country
senses.definitionCN: 野外 rough 的小径或道路
senses.example: They took a narrow mountain track to the village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们沿狭窄的山间小路走向村庄。
senses.why: Any line of repeated footprints becomes a path people reuse.
senses.whyCN: 反复踩出的脚印线自然变成人们重复使用的路。

senses.title: To follow someone or something by signs
senses.definition: to follow the movements of a person, animal, or object by finding evidence
senses.definitionCN: 通过线索跟随人、动物或物体的移动
senses.example: Scientists track the migration of birds by satellite.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家用卫星追踪候鸟迁徙。
senses.why: If a trail shows where something went, following the trail is tracking it.
senses.whyCN: 既然踪迹显示去向，顺着踪迹走就是追踪。

senses.title: To record and follow progress
senses.definition: to record and follow the development or position of something over time
senses.definitionCN: 持续记录并关注事物的发展或位置
senses.example: The app tracks how many hours you sleep every night.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用记录你每晚睡了多少小时。
senses.why: Following physical tracks extends to following figures and changes on a screen.
senses.whyCN: 跟随实体踪迹延伸为跟随屏幕上的数据与变化。

intro.en: Track came into English in the late Middle Ages, generally assumed from Old French trac or a Germanic source, and originally meant a line or course drawn by something passing.
intro.cn: track 于中世纪晚期进入英语，一般认为源自古法语 trac 或日耳曼语源，本义是经过者拉出的线或路径。

items.en: The source is usually cited as Old French trac or a Germanic root meaning to draw or pull.
items.cn: 一般认为词源是古法语 trac 或日耳曼词根，意为「拉、拖」。

items.en: Recorded as a line or course, such as the course of a ship or animal.
items.cn: 中古英语记作轨迹、路径，如船只或动物的行进路线。

items.en: Extended to rails for vehicles and prepared running courses.
items.cn: 扩展到车辆铁轨和专门修建的跑道。

items.en: The verb developed the senses of following animals and, later, monitoring data.
items.cn: 动词发展出追猎动物、进而监测数据的义项。

items.en: The competing Old French and Germanic accounts are not finally settled.
items.cn: 古法语与日耳曼两种来源假说尚未有定论。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to track, and words in the pursuit field.
note.cn: 与 track 形近音近的词，以及同属追踪义场的词。

entries.definition: a small nail or a change of direction

entries.definition: a clever act meant to deceive
entries.definitionCN: 诡计；戏法，与 track 发音相近，词源无关

entries.definition: a path or a line of marks left behind
entries.definitionCN: 小径；拖出的痕迹，与 track 近义但更强调拖拽痕迹

entries.definition: a way made for walking
entries.definitionCN: 道路；小径，人工修建的通行路

entries.definition: to find someone or something by investigating
entries.definitionCN: 追查；查找，强调通过调查找到

entries.definition: a planned way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 路线；既定路径，强调规划而非痕迹

normalIntro.en: Link the sound to the mark left on the ground.
normalIntro.cn: 把发音与地面上留下的痕迹连起来。

normal.en: a truck leaves a track
normal.cn: 卡车（truck）驶过会留下轨迹（track），一音之差

normal.en: collocation: on the right track
normal.cn: 常用搭配 on the right track（思路正确）

normal.cn: keep track of＝随时掌握动态

normal.en: track record = past performance
normal.cn: track record＝过往成绩单，赛跑道上的历史

normal.en: railway track, running track
normal.cn: 铁轨与跑道是 track 的两个高频场景

abstract.en: See a line of footprints stretching across fresh snow
abstract.cn: 看见一串脚印横过新雪

abstract.en: Losing track of time is like losing the path you walked
abstract.cn: 忘了时间就像弄丢了走过的路

abstract.en: The train never leaves its track; stay on yours
abstract.cn: 列车从不出轨，你也守住自己的轨道

examples.en: The hunters found fresh tiger tracks near the river.
examples.cn: 猎人在河边发现了新鲜的老虎足迹。

examples.en: The radar system can track hundreds of planes at once.
examples.cn: 雷达系统可以同时追踪数百架飞机。

examples.en: After two wrong answers she was finally on the right track.
examples.cn: 答错两次之后，她终于思路对头了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tracked」——想象卡车（truck）压过雪地，留下一条 track（轨迹）。truck 少个 r，track 少个 u，认准 ck 结尾。

root: 一般认为源自古法语 trac 或日耳曼词根「拉、拖」，本义为经过者拉出的线，后引申为轨道、小路和追踪行为。两种来源假说并列，未最终定论。

sensesIntro.en: From marks left on the ground, the word grew into rails, paths, following, and monitoring.
sensesIntro.cn: 从地面留下的痕迹生长出铁轨、小路、追踪与监测诸义。
